+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction.Observables
+
+/-!
+# Consistency of the pulled-apart Pauli measurements
+
+This module records the two estimates by which the polynomial marginals absorb
+the expanded point measurements, with all heterogeneous placements written
+explicitly. It also states the consistency of the pulled-apart
+measurements with the original point measurements and the self-consistency of
+the corresponding observables.
+
+## References
+
+The marginal estimates formalize `lem:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:213-244`, from
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1609-1664`.
+The remaining declarations formalize `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis` in
+blueprint lines 127-195, from paper lines 1458-1608.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-! ## Absorption of expanded point measurements -/
+
+/-- The polynomial marginal and the opposite player's expanded point
+measurement resolve the identity on average. Quantification over the directed
+opposite-placement relation gives all four instances of the source's
+symmetric-equivalents clause.
+
+This is Equation `eq:qld-sg-cons` of
+`lem:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:213-227`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1609-1635`.
+
+The source absorbs constant factors and the game error into `deltaS`. Here
+`deltaG` is the raw global-witness error, and `deltaConstructPaulis` records
+that enlargement explicitly.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the agreement calculation converting
+`GlobalPairWitness.point_consistent_alice`, its Bob-side counterpart, and the
+register-placement transfers into all four identity estimates. -/
+theorem sum_marginalPoly_pointMeas_approx_id :
+    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
+      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon deltaG : ℝ),
+        0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ deltaG →
+          ∀ (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
+            (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind)
+            (p₁ p₂ : Placement), p₁.IsOpposite p₂ →
+              opDistSq (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
+                (fun u => ∑ g : Poly P,
+                  S.place p₁ ((w.marginalPoly p₁.side W).effect g) *
+                    S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side W u).effect
+                      (MvPolynomial.eval u g.1)))
+                (fun _ => 1) S.psiHat ≤
+                  deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon deltaG P.m P.d P.q := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Each polynomial marginal annihilates the complement of the corresponding
+same-side expanded point effect on average. The answer summation is over the
+polynomial outcome, and quantification over `Placement` gives all four
+single-party symmetric equivalents.
+
+This is Equation `eq:qld-sg-cons2` of
+`lem:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:213-227`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1617-1662`.
+
+The explicit `deltaConstructPaulis` bound retains the point-measurement error
+which the source absorbs into its adjusted `deltaS`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the projection-contraction and expanded
+point self-consistency calculation on every placement at paper lines
+1637-1662. -/
+theorem marginalPoly_sub_pointMeas_approx_zero :
+    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
+      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon deltaG : ℝ),
+        0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ deltaG →
+          ∀ (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
+            (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind) (p : Placement),
+            opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
+              (fun u g =>
+                S.place p ((w.marginalPoly p.side W).effect g) *
+                  (1 - S.place p ((S.pointMeasExp p.side W u).effect
+                    (MvPolynomial.eval u g.1))))
+              (fun _ _ => 0) S.psiHat ≤
+                deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon deltaG P.m P.d P.q := by
+  sorry
+
+/-! ## Non-encoding support -/
+
+/-- The state-dependent mass assigned by a side's polynomial marginal to
+outcomes outside the low-degree encoding image.  The finite support filter is
+written explicitly so the restricted decoder identity is never applied to an
+arbitrary polynomial representative.
+
+This is the left-hand side of `eq:qld-nonencoding-mass` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:170-173`, from
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1458-1602`.
+The bound remains a proposition-valued proof obligation, as required by
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
+noncomputable def nonencodingMarginalMass {P : AdmissibleParams}
+    {epsilon deltaS : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
+    (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaS) (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ := by
+  classical
+  exact ∑ g ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun g : Poly P => ¬ IsEncoding g),
+    (inner ℂ S.psiHat
+      (applyOperatorToState
+        (S.placeSide side
+          (heteroKron ((w.marginalPoly side W).effect g)
+            (1 : Op (PauliRegister P))))
+        S.psiHat)).re
+
+/-- The non-encoding support estimate required by the Chapter 16 extraction
+argument. For either player side and either Pauli basis, the marginal mass on
+polynomial representatives outside the encoding image is bounded by the
+common construction error.
+
+This is the named obligation for `eq:qld-nonencoding-mass`, blueprint
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:170-173`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1458-1602`.
+The estimate is intentionally not folded into a decoder identity; its proof
+must use the point-consistency hypotheses and Schwartz--Zippel. See
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks this support estimate. -/
+theorem nonencodingMarginalMass_le :
+    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
+      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon deltaG : ℝ),
+        0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ deltaG →
+          ∀ (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
+            (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG)
+            (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind),
+            nonencodingMarginalMass w side W ≤
+              deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon deltaG P.m P.d P.q := by
+  sorry
+
+/-! ## Consistency of the pulled-apart measurements -/
+
+/-- Alice's original point measurement is consistent with Bob's pulled-apart
+measurement on average over uniformly random points. This is the first display
+of Item 1 in `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:127-154`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1463-1492`.
+
+The source reuses `deltaS` after absorbing the non-encoding and game-error
+terms. The Lean conclusion keeps the raw witness error `deltaG` separate in
+`deltaConstructPaulis`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the non-encoding-mass estimate required
+by the restricted decoder identity; see
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`. -/
+theorem tildeM_consistent_pointMeas :
+    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
+      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon deltaG : ℝ),
+        0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ deltaG →
+          ∀ (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
+            (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind),
+            consistencyDefect
+              (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
+              (fun u a =>
+                S.placePlayer .alice ((S.pointMeas .alice W u).effect a))
+              (fun u a => S.placeSide .bob
+                (tildeM w .bob W (indicatorVec u) a))
+              S.psiHat ≤
+                deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon deltaG P.m P.d P.q := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Alice's pulled-apart measurement is consistent with Bob's original point
+measurement on average over uniformly random points. This is the
+register-interchanged display of Item 1 in `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`,
+blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:127-154`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1463-1492`.
+
+The conclusion uses the same explicit construction scale as the first player
+ordering.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the player-interchanged
+non-encoding-mass argument. -/
+theorem tildeM_consistent_pointMeas' :
+    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
+      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon deltaG : ℝ),
+        0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ deltaG →
+          ∀ (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
+            (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind),
+            consistencyDefect
+              (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
+              (fun u a => S.placeSide .alice
+                (tildeM w .alice W (indicatorVec u) a))
+              (fun u a =>
+                S.placePlayer .bob ((S.pointMeas .bob W u).effect a))
+              S.psiHat ≤
+                deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon deltaG P.m P.d P.q := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The pulled-apart observables on Alice's and Bob's extraction blocks are
+self-consistent on average over the uniformly random Pauli register. This is
+Item 2 of `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:127-154`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1476-1605`.
+
+The construction scale exposes the square-root game error and
+Schwartz--Zippel loss that the source absorbs into `deltaS`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the pulling-consistency calculation and
+the final trace postprocessing from measurements to observables. -/
+theorem tildeObs_selfConsistent :
+    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
+      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon deltaG : ℝ),
+        0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ deltaG →
+          ∀ (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
+            (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG) (W : PauliKind)
+            (j : Fin P.model.basisDim),
+            opDistSq (uniformDistribution (PauliRegister P))
+              (fun u => S.placeSide .alice (tildeObs w .alice W u j))
+              (fun u => S.placeSide .bob (tildeObs w .bob W u j))
+              S.psiHat ≤
+                deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon deltaG P.m P.d P.q := by
+  sorry
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

@@ -0,0 +1,262 @@
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Observables.ExpandedDefs
+
+/-!
+# Extraction foundations
+
+This module supplies the witness-independent register bookkeeping used to pull
+the Pauli measurements apart. It retains the distinct local spaces of a
+heterogeneous strategy, coarse-grains the generalized Pauli projectors by a
+dot product, and records the state and error expressions needed by the later
+extraction witness.
+
+The binary phases use the existing `phaseSign`; the fixed field basis remains
+the basis stored in `P.model` and is not re-quantified here.
+
+## References
+
+The Pauli dot-product projectors formalize `def:tau-dot-product-projector` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:46-53`, from
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`.
+The register and state helpers support `def:tilde-m-measurement`,
+`def:v-swap-unitary`, and `lem:qld-unitary`, from paper lines 1429-1435 and
+1666-1713 and blueprint lines 55-62 and 203-260.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-! ## Heterogeneous extraction registers -/
+
+/-- One player's registers after adjoining the two generalized-Pauli
+registers: `AA'A''` or `BB'B''`. This identifies the register order and spaces for
+paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1429-1435,1687-1713` and
+blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:55-62,203-230`. -/
+abbrev ExtractionBlock (P : AdmissibleParams) (ι : Type*) :=
+  (ι × PauliRegister P) × PauliRegister P
+
+/-- The two heterogeneous extraction blocks in the order
+`AA'A'' | BB'B''`. This is the block presentation of the existing `SixReg`
+space used in `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
+abbrev ExtractionRegisters (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
+  ExtractionBlock P ιA × ExtractionBlock P ιB
+
+/-- The auxiliary registers `AA'BB'` occurring before the extracted EPR
+factor in `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`,
+paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
+abbrev ExtractionAuxRegisters (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
+  (ιA × PauliRegister P) × (ιB × PauliRegister P)
+
+/-- Reassociate the landed six-register order with the two extraction blocks.
+This equivalence identifies the register order in paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1429-1435,1687-1713`. -/
+def sixRegExtractionEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
+    SixReg P ιA ιB ≃ ExtractionRegisters P ιA ιB where
+  toFun p := (((p.1.1, p.1.2.1), p.1.2.2),
+    ((p.2.1, p.2.2.1), p.2.2.2))
+  invFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.1.2, p.1.2)),
+    (p.2.1.1, (p.2.1.2, p.2.2)))
+  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
+  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
+
+/-- Shuffle `AA'BB' | A''B''` into the landed six-register order. This is
+Lean-only bookkeeping for the ideal state in `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
+def extractionIdealShuffle (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
+    (ExtractionAuxRegisters P ιA ιB ×
+      (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
+  toFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.1.2, p.2.1)),
+    (p.1.2.1, (p.1.2.2, p.2.2)))
+  invFun p := (((p.1.1, p.1.2.1), (p.2.1, p.2.2.1)),
+    (p.1.2.2, p.2.2.2))
+  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
+  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
+
+namespace ProjectiveSetting
+
+variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
+
+/-- Place an operator on one complete extraction block, with the identity on
+the other player's block. This is the heterogeneous Lean realization of the
+side-qualified operators in paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1429-1435,1687-1713`. -/
+noncomputable def placeSide (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (O : Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side))) :
+    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
+  cases side with
+  | alice =>
+      exact reindexOp
+        (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
+        (heteroKron O 1)
+  | bob =>
+      exact reindexOp
+        (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
+        (heteroKron 1 O)
+
+/-- Lift an operator on a player's original strategy register to that player's
+full extraction block. This is Lean-only support for the raw Pauli and point
+measurements in `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis` and `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:105-124,245-260`. -/
+noncomputable def onPlayer (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (O : Op (S.LocalSpace side)) :
+    Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
+  heteroKron (heteroKron O 1) 1
+
+/-- Place an operator on the original strategy register of the selected
+player. This helper uses the landed `ProjectiveSetting.place` API and is
+Lean-only support for the player-side conclusions of `lem:qld-unitary`,
+blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`. -/
+noncomputable def placePlayer (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (O : Op (S.LocalSpace side)) :
+    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
+  cases side with
+  | alice => exact S.place .AA' (heteroKron O 1)
+  | bob => exact S.place .BB' (heteroKron O 1)
+
+/-- Place an operator on the selected extracted register `A''` or `B''`.
+The unused strategy register in the landed crossed placement is assigned the
+identity. This is Lean-only support for the ideal Pauli operators in
+`lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
+noncomputable def placeExtractedRegister (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (O : Op (PauliRegister P)) :
+    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
+  cases side with
+  | alice =>
+      exact S.place .BA'' (heteroKron (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) O)
+  | bob =>
+      exact S.place .AB'' (heteroKron (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) O)
+
+/-- Place a pair of block operators simultaneously on `AA'A''` and
+`BB'B''`. This is Lean-only support for the transformed state in
+`lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
+noncomputable def placeBoth (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+    (VA : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
+    (VB : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
+    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
+  reindexOp (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
+    (heteroKron VA VB)
+
+/-- Apply one operator to each heterogeneous extraction block. This is the
+witness-independent state transformation used for `V_A tensor V_B` in
+`lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
+noncomputable def applyBoth (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+    (VA : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
+    (VB : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB))
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ
+      (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
+    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
+  applyOperatorToState (S.placeBoth VA VB) ψ
+
+/-- The state `aux tensor EPR_q^{tensor M}` in the landed six-register order.
+This is the ideal state in Item 1 of `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
+noncomputable def idealExpState (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ
+      (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
+    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
+  classical
+  exact
+    reindexState (extractionIdealShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
+      (vecTensor aux (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
+
+end ProjectiveSetting
+
+/-! ## Coarse-grained Pauli projectors -/
+
+/-- Coarse-grain a finite operator family along a map of outcomes. This is the
+operator-valued sum corresponding to `Measurement.postprocess`, used by
+`def:tau-dot-product-projector`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:46-53`. -/
+noncomputable def bracketOp {α β ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq β]
+    (N : α → Op ι) (f : α → β) (b : β) : Op ι :=
+  ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), N a
+
+/-- The effect of a postprocessed measurement is the corresponding
+coarse-grained operator sum. This equality is used by `def:bracket` and
+`def:tau-dot-product-projector`, blueprint
+`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26` and `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:46-53`. -/
+theorem postprocess_effect_eq_bracketOp {α β ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : Measurement α ι) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
+    (M.postprocess f).effect b = bracketOp M.effect f b :=
+  rfl
+
+/-- The projector obtained by measuring in basis `W` and retaining outcomes
+whose dot product with `u` is `a`. This is Equation `eq:def-tauwu` in
+`def:tau-dot-product-projector`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:46-53`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`. -/
+noncomputable def tauDotProj {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)
+    (u : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Op (PauliRegister P) :=
+  bracketOp (pauliProj W) (fun h => dotProduct h u) a
+
+/-- Each dot-product coarse-graining is a projector, as asserted in
+`def:tau-dot-product-projector`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:46-53`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the orthogonal rank-one Pauli projector
+calculation. -/
+theorem tauDotProj_isProj {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)
+    (u : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
+    IsProj (tauDotProj W u a) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- For fixed `W` and `u`, the dot-product projectors sum to the identity.
+This is the completeness assertion of `def:tau-dot-product-projector`,
+blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:46-53`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks completeness of the generalized-Pauli
+projector family. -/
+theorem sum_tauDotProj_eq_one {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)
+    (u : PauliRegister P) :
+    ∑ a : PauliScalar P, tauDotProj W u a = 1 := by
+  sorry
+
+/-! ## Conjugation and extraction error -/
+
+/-- Conjugation of an operator by a square matrix. This is Lean-only notation
+for the exact conjugation equations in `lem:v-swap-conjugation`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:216-230`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1687-1713`. -/
+noncomputable def conjBy {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
+    (V N : Op ι) : Op ι :=
+  V * N * Vᴴ
+
+/-- The common error scale for constructing the pulled-apart measurements from
+a global polynomial-pair witness. Here `deltaG` is the raw consistency error of
+the global witness. The remaining terms record the point-measurement transfer
+and the Schwartz--Zippel loss; when `0 ≤ epsilon ≤ 1`, `sqrt epsilon` also
+dominates terms of order `epsilon`.
+
+This makes explicit the enlargement of the error called `deltaS` in
+`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:120-196`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1458-1605`. -/
+noncomputable def deltaConstructPaulis (C epsilon deltaG : ℝ)
+    (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
+  C * (deltaG + Real.sqrt epsilon +
+    ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))
+
+/-- The explicit extraction scale
+`C * (deltaS^(1/4) + md/q)` from `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
+noncomputable def deltaExtract (C deltaS : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
+  C * (Real.rpow deltaS (1 / 4 : ℝ) + ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.Decoding
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Witnesses
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction.Defs
+
+/-!
+# Pulled-apart Pauli observables
+
+This module constructs the measurements and observables used to pull the two
+Pauli bases onto separate registers. The construction retains the distinct
+local spaces of the two players and uses the binary basis fixed in the
+canonical field model.
+
+## References
+
+The product form and observable relations formalize `lem:tildew-product-form`
+in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:75-88`, from
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1415-1456`.
+The swap identities formalize
+`lem:v-swap-conjugation`, blueprint lines 208-243 and paper lines 1687-1713.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-! ## Pulled-apart measurements and observables -/
+
+namespace PauliKind
+
+/-- Select the polynomial belonging to a Pauli basis from a joint polynomial
+outcome. This is the marginalization used at paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1421-1423` and blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:35-44`. -/
+def selectPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind) : PolyPair P -> Poly P
+  | pair => match W with
+    | .X => pair.1
+    | .Z => pair.2
+
+end PauliKind
+
+namespace GlobalPairWitness
+
+/-- The single-basis marginal of the global polynomial-pair measurement.
+This is `def:s-w-marginals`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:35-44`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1421-1423`. -/
+noncomputable def marginalPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) :
+    Measurement (Poly P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
+  (w.Smeas side).postprocess W.selectPoly
+
+/-- The single-basis marginal remains a projective measurement. This is the
+projectivity assertion implicit in `def:s-w-marginals`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:35-44`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1421-1423`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the preservation of projectivity under
+the finite postprocessing map `PauliKind.selectPoly`. -/
+theorem marginalPoly_isProjective {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) :
+    Measurement.IsProjective (w.marginalPoly side W) := by
+  sorry
+
+end GlobalPairWitness
+
+/-- The pulled-apart projective-measurement effect from Equation `eq:tilde_M`.
+The polynomial marginal acts on the player's expanded local space and the
+dot-product projector acts on the newly adjoined register. Blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:55-62`; paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1425-1435`. -/
+noncomputable def tildeM {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
+    (a : PauliScalar P) : Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
+  ∑ g : Poly P,
+    heteroKron ((w.marginalPoly side W).effect g)
+      (tauDotProj W u (dotProduct (decodeFq g) u - a))
+
+/-- Each pulled-apart effect is a projector, as asserted in
+`def:tilde-m-measurement`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:55-62`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1425-1435`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the orthogonal-sum calculation using
+`marginalPoly_isProjective` and `tauDotProj_isProj`. -/
+theorem tildeM_isProj {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
+    (a : PauliScalar P) :
+    IsProj (tildeM w side W u a) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The pulled-apart effects are complete for each fixed basis and Pauli
+register vector. This is the completeness assertion in
+`def:tilde-m-measurement`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:55-62`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1425-1435`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks summing the orthogonal dot-product
+projectors and the polynomial marginal effects. -/
+theorem sum_tildeM_eq_one {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P) :
+    ∑ a : PauliScalar P, tildeM w side W u a = 1 := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The binary observable obtained from the trace coarse-graining of `tildeM`.
+This is Equation `eq:def-tildewj` in `def:tilde-w-observables`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:64-71`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1437-1442`. -/
+noncomputable def tildeObs {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
+    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) : Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
+  ∑ a : PauliScalar P,
+    phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a)) •
+      tildeM w side W u a
+
+/-- Product form of the pulled-apart observable, Equation
+`eq:tildewj-product-form` of `lem:tildew-product-form`. Blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:75-88`; paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1442-1450`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the finite Fourier regrouping needed to
+derive this equality from `tauObservable_eq_sum_pauliProj`. Discharge: expand
+the two finite sums and reindex the Pauli outcomes by their dot product. -/
+theorem tildeObs_eq_heteroKron {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
+    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
+    tildeObs w side W u j =
+      heteroKron
+        (∑ pair : PolyPair P,
+          phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model
+            (P.model.basis j * dotProduct (decodeFq (W.selectPoly pair)) u)) •
+            (w.Smeas side).effect pair)
+        (tauObservable W (P.model.basis j • u)) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Every pulled-apart observable is Hermitian, as asserted in
+`lem:tildew-product-form`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:75-88`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1450`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks this consequence of the product form.
+Discharge: use projectivity of `w.Smeas side` and Hermiticity of the generalized
+Pauli observable. -/
+theorem tildeObs_isHermitian {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
+    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
+    (tildeObs w side W u j).IsHermitian := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Every pulled-apart observable squares to the identity, as asserted in
+`lem:tildew-product-form`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:75-88`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1450`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks this consequence of the product form.
+Discharge: eliminate cross terms using the orthogonality of `w.Smeas side` and
+use that `tauObservable` is self-inverse. -/
+theorem tildeObs_mul_self {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
+    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
+    tildeObs w side W u j * tildeObs w side W u j = 1 := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The corrected twisted commutation relation for pulled-apart observables.
+This is Equation `eq:tildew-twisted-commutation` in blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:82-87`, correcting paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1451-1456`.
+
+**Local fix:** the paper drops this phase when `j != j'`, which is false for
+general register vectors; see `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_cross-basis-phase.tex`.
+Issue #47 tracks the proof. Discharge: combine both product forms with
+`tauObservable_X_mul_Z`. -/
+theorem tildeObs_twisted_commutation {P : AdmissibleParams}
+    {epsilon delta : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
+    (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (u v : PauliRegister P) (j j' : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
+    tildeObs w side .X u j * tildeObs w side .Z v j' =
+      phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model
+        (P.model.basis j * P.model.basis j' * dotProduct u v)) •
+        (tildeObs w side .Z v j' * tildeObs w side .X u j) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-! ## Swap conjugation -/
+
+/-- The swap map built from the global polynomial-pair measurement, with the
+crossed decoded arguments required by `def:v-swap-unitary`. Blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:208-215`; paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1687-1700`. -/
+noncomputable def swapUnitary {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) : Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
+  ∑ pair : PolyPair P,
+    heteroKron ((w.Smeas side).effect pair)
+      (tauObservable .X (decodeFq pair.2) *
+        tauObservable .Z (decodeFq pair.1))
+
+/-- The swap map is a right unitary. This is the first exact unitarity
+calculation of `lem:v-swap-conjugation`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:219-226`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1687-1699`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the finite projector calculation.
+Discharge: use projectivity and completeness of `w.Smeas side` together with
+self-inverseness of both generalized Pauli observables. -/
+theorem swapUnitary_mul_conjTranspose {P : AdmissibleParams}
+    {epsilon delta : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
+    (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta) (side : PlayerSide) :
+    swapUnitary w side * (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ = 1 := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The swap map is a left unitary. This is the reverse exact unitarity
+calculation implicit in `lem:v-swap-conjugation`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:219-226`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1687-1699`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the reverse projector calculation.
+Discharge: use the same orthogonality and Pauli involution identities as in
+`swapUnitary_mul_conjTranspose`. -/
+theorem conjTranspose_mul_swapUnitary {P : AdmissibleParams}
+    {epsilon delta : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
+    (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta) (side : PlayerSide) :
+    (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ * swapUnitary w side = 1 := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Exact conjugation of a pulled-apart observable by the swap map. This is
+Equation `eq:v-swap-obs-conjugation` in `lem:v-swap-conjugation`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:219-226`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1701-1713`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the diagonal projector reduction.
+Discharge: substitute `tildeObs_eq_heteroKron`, eliminate off-diagonal outcomes,
+and cancel the phase using `tauObservable_X_mul_Z`. -/
+theorem swapUnitary_conj_tildeObs {P : AdmissibleParams}
+    {epsilon delta : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
+    (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta) (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind)
+    (u : PauliRegister P) (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
+    conjBy (swapUnitary w side) (tildeObs w side W u j) =
+      heteroKron (1 : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side))
+        (tauObservable W (P.model.basis j • u)) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Exact conjugation of a pulled-apart point effect by the swap map. This is
+Equation `eq:qld-unitary-6` in `lem:v-swap-conjugation`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:227-233`; its calculation occurs at paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1805-1822`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the exact relabeling calculation.
+Discharge: expand `tildeM`, conjugate each Pauli projector, and translate the
+dot-product constraint with `lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct`; no unrestricted
+decoder interpolation identity is used. -/
+theorem swapUnitary_conj_tildeM {P : AdmissibleParams}
+    {epsilon delta : ℝ} {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
+    (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta) (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind)
+    (u : Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
+    conjBy (swapUnitary w side) (tildeM w side W (indicatorVec u) a) =
+      heteroKron (1 : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side))
+        (bracketOp (pauliProj W) (fun h => lowDegreeEnc h u) a) := by
+  sorry
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction.Consistency
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.Soundness
+
+/-!
+# Extraction by the swap unitaries
+
+The concrete swap operators below yield the Pauli extraction conclusion. The
+local maps are constructed from the global polynomial
+measurements, and all operators retain the heterogeneous Alice and Bob
+placements. The generalized Pauli projectors use the field and basis fixed by
+`P.model`.
+
+## References
+
+The extraction witness formalizes `lem:qld-unitary` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:295-314`, from
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1860`.
+The error-form comparison records `rem:pauli-robustness-form`, blueprint lines
+380-385 and paper lines 1855-1858 and 1868-1876.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- The concrete conclusion of `lem:qld-unitary`: the two swap maps extract an
+EPR state and conjugate each player's total Pauli measurement to the canonical
+Pauli projectors. The answer sum in `pauli_close` is over
+`PauliRegister P`; the uniform distribution on `Unit` records that there is no
+average over questions.
+
+Blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:295-314`; paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685,1827-1859`. The swap maps
+are `swapUnitary w .alice` and `swapUnitary w .bob`, defined from the
+side-indexed global measurements, and use only the basis fixed by `P.model`.
+-/
+structure ExtractionWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaS : ℝ}
+    (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon) (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaS)
+    (delta : ℝ) where
+  /-- Each swap map is a right unitary. -/
+  swap_right_unitary : ∀ side : PlayerSide,
+    swapUnitary w side * (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ = 1
+  /-- Each swap map is a left unitary. -/
+  swap_left_unitary : ∀ side : PlayerSide,
+    (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ * swapUnitary w side = 1
+  /-- The auxiliary state on registers `AA'BB'`. -/
+  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ
+    (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
+  /-- The auxiliary state is normalized. -/
+  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
+  /-- Applying both concrete swap maps to the expanded state extracts the ideal
+  auxiliary-state/EPR tensor product. -/
+  state_close :
+    ‖S.applyBoth (swapUnitary w .alice) (swapUnitary w .bob) S.psiHat -
+        S.idealExpState aux‖ ^ 2 ≤ delta
+  /-- On the ideal extracted state, conjugated total-Pauli effects are close to
+  the canonical projectors, for both players and both Pauli bases. -/
+  pauli_close : ∀ (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind),
+    opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
+      (fun (_ : Unit) (h : PauliRegister P) =>
+        conjBy (S.placeSide side (swapUnitary w side))
+          (S.placePlayer side ((S.pauliMeas side W).effect h)))
+      (fun (_ : Unit) (h : PauliRegister P) =>
+        S.placeExtractedRegister side (pauliProj W h))
+      (S.idealExpState aux) ≤ delta
+
+/-- `lem:qld-unitary`: the concrete swap maps admit extraction data at the
+explicit extraction scale applied to `deltaConstructPaulis`.
+
+This is the source-facing existence statement from blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:295-314` and paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1860`. It introduces no transfer
+premise or additional basis parameter.
+
+**Local fix:** the positive-contraction estimate and normalization case split
+repair the two numerical defects at paper lines 1743-1783 without changing the
+conclusion; see `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_extraction-transfer.tex`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the EPR projection argument and the
+Schwartz-Zippel comparison at paper lines 1715-1858. Discharge: construct
+`aux` from the EPR projection of the swapped state, use the corrected
+small-error case split, and combine the point-measurement consistency with the
+exact swap conjugation identities. -/
+theorem exists_extractionWitness :
+    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
+      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon deltaG : ℝ),
+        0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ deltaG →
+          ∀ (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
+            (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG),
+            Nonempty
+              (ExtractionWitness S w
+                (deltaExtract C
+                  (deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon deltaG P.m P.d P.q)
+                  P.m P.d P.q)) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The composed construction and extraction errors preserve the error family
+of `thm:pauli`: when `deltaG` has the form
+`deltaQld a b epsilon m d q`, the result is bounded by another member of that
+family after decreasing the exponent and enlarging the universal constant.
+
+This is the named quantitative obligation behind
+`rem:pauli-robustness-form`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:380-385`, and the concluding comparison at paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1855-1858,1868-1876`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks this real-power estimate. Discharge:
+take an exponent no larger than `b / 4` and `1 / 8`, bound the fourth root of
+the terms in `deltaConstructPaulis`, absorb `md/q` using admissibility, and
+enlarge the prefactor and polynomial exponent. -/
+theorem deltaExtract_le_deltaQld (C a b : ℝ) (hC : 1 ≤ C) (ha : 1 < a)
+    (hb : 0 < b) (hb1 : b < 1) :
+    ∃ a' b' : ℝ, 1 ≤ a' ∧ 0 < b' ∧ b' < 1 ∧
+      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon : ℝ), 0 ≤ epsilon →
+        epsilon ≤ 1 →
+        deltaExtract C
+            (deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon
+              (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) P.m P.d P.q)
+            P.m P.d P.q ≤
+          deltaQld a' b' epsilon P.m P.d P.q := by
+  sorry
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    41	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    42	\[
    43	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    44	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    45	\]
    46	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    47	\[
    48	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    49	  \qquad
    50	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    51	\]
    52	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    53	\[
    54	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    55	\]
    56	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    57	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    58	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    59	
    60	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    61	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    62	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    63	\[
    64	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    65	\]
    66	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    67	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    68	$\Delta$.

    70	\section{Numerical defects in the source proof}
    71	
    72	Lines~1715--1742 of
    73	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    74	construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
    75	estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
    76	$\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
    77	source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
    78	\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
    79	small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
    80	$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
    81	
    82	The triangle inequality yields
    83	\[
    84	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
    85	\]
    86	so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
    87	$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
    88	$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
    89	universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
    90	vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
    91	are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.
    92	
    93	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    94	
    95	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    96	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    97	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
    98	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
    99	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   100	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   101	
   102	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   103	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   104	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   105	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   106	\[
   107	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   108	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   109	\]
   110	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   111	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   112	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   113	
   114	This transfer is an open proof obligation for the next extraction stage.  It
   115	must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
   116	estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,
   117	residual assumption, or hypothesis of the source-labelled soundness theorem.

   116	\section{The source assertion and the two routes}
   117	
   118	The source proof in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} constructs $\hat Q^{\ell}_f$ by
   119	averaging, over a distribution $D$ on tuples $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$
   120	provided by its sub-line lemma, the pushforward of
   121	$T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}$ along a combining map, and reduces the lemma to a
   122	bound on the scalar consistency defect
   123	\begin{equation}
   124	  \Lambda \,=\,
   125	  \E_{(\ell,\ell_X,\ell_Z) \sim D}\
   126	  \E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta) \in \ell}
   127	  \sum_{f_X,f_Z} \bra{\hat\psi}
   128	  \big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \ot
   129	  \big(\Id - \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{f_X(x),f_Z(z)}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}
   130	  \ket{\hat\psi}\,,
   131	  \tag{\path{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency}}
   132	\end{equation}
   133	in which the point $(x,z,\alpha,\beta)$ is uniform on $\ell$ and the sum
   134	ranges over pairs of line polynomials.  The proof then bounds $\Lambda$
   135	twice, by different routes and with different results, and the printed
   136	record is internally inconsistent: the display introducing $\Lambda$
   137	asserts the first-route bound, while the closing lines assert the
   138	second-route bound as the operative one; the lemma statement claims a
   139	third form matching neither.
   140	
   141	\paragraph{The first route.}
   142	Three claims are chained.  The combined point measurement
   143	$\hat Q^{x,z}$ is replaced by the ordered product of the two point
   144	measurements at cost $\delta_Q^{1/2}$; the $X$-point factor is removed at
   145	cost $m\,\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}$; and the remaining $Z$-point
   146	correlation is shown to be within
   147	$\sqrt{m}\,(\delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4} + \eps^{1/4})$ of one.  The
   148	factors of $m$ enter through the mixture structure of the sub-line
   149	distribution: each restricted line distribution carries mixture weight
   150	$1/(2m)$ in the line-point distribution, so an average bounded by
   151	$\delta$ over the full distribution is bounded only by $2m\delta$ over a
   152	restricted component and by $4m^2\delta$ over a product of two
   153	components, and the Cauchy--Schwarz steps halve the exponents.  Chaining
   154	the claims gives
   155	\begin{equation*}
   156	  \Lambda \,=\, O\big(m\,(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4}
   157	  + \delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2})\big)
   158	  \,=\, m \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)\,.
   159	\end{equation*}
   160	One intermediate assertion needs a harmless correction: the final line
   161	of the proof of the second claim asserts the bound
   162	$O(m^2 \delta_{\mathrm{Line}})$ for a consistency term that is close to
   163	one, rather than for its deficit.  Read as a bound on the deficit ---
   164	which is what the surrounding Cauchy--Schwarz argument requires and what
   165	the invoked line--point consistency provides after the mixture
   166	inflation --- the claim and its use are correct, with the square root of
   167	the deficit giving the stated cost $m\,\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}$.
   168	
   169	\paragraph{The second route.}
   170	After the chain, the source restarts: it asserts that, by Property~2 of
   171	its sub-line lemma, $\Lambda$ is a mixture, over types
   172	$\mathrm{v}_1, \mathrm{v}_2 \in \{\mathrm{ALine}, \mathrm{DLine}\}$ and
   173	indices $i, j \in \{1, \dots, m\}$, of terms
   174	\begin{equation*}
   175	  \E_{(\ell_X, x) \sim D_{\mathrm{v}_1,i}}\
   176	  \E_{(\ell_Z, z) \sim D_{\mathrm{v}_2,j}}
   177	  \sum_{f_X,f_Z} \bra{\hat\psi}
   178	  \big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \ot
   179	  \big(\Id - \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{f_X(x),f_Z(z)}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}
   180	  \ket{\hat\psi}
   181	\end{equation*}
   182	over two \emph{independently} sampled restricted line-point pairs,
   183	bounds each term by $O(m^2\delta_P)$ using the restricted-distribution
   184	consequence of the two-basis line lemma, and concludes
   185	$\Lambda = O(m^2\delta_P)$.  The invoked decomposition concerns the
   186	\emph{joint} law of the pair $((\ell_X, x), (\ell_Z, z))$, where $x$ and
   187	$z$ are the two blocks of the single point sampled on $\ell$.  Property~2
   188	of the sub-line lemma does not assert this joint law: it asserts the
   189	component-wise product law of the pair of \emph{lines}
   190	$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, and the conditional uniformity of each point on its
   191	line separately --- equivalently, the laws of the two pairs
   192	$((\ell_X, x), (\ell_Z, z'))$ and $((\ell_X, x'), (\ell_Z, z))$ in which
   193	the \emph{other} point is resampled independently.  These marginal
   194	statements are exactly what the first route's claims consume, each
   195	involving one point at a time; the joint decomposition used by the
   196	second route is a strictly stronger property and is not established by
   197	the lemma it is attributed to.
   198	
   199	\section{Why neither route yields the stated form}
   200	
   201	The stated error form is $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, a function of the two
   202	quantities $m^2\eps$ and $md/q$ that vanishes as both vanish.  The
   203	first-route bound is not dominated by any such function: along the
   204	scaling $\eps = m^{-4}$ with $q/(md) \to \infty$, both $m^2\eps = m^{-2}$
   205	and $md/q$ tend to $0$, while the term $m\,\eps^{1/4} = 1$ does not.
   206	Hence the established derivation supports no bound of the claimed form.
   207	The second-route bound, even granting the missing decomposition, carries
   208	the separate prefactor $m^2$: writing $\delta_P = \poly(\eps, md/q)$
   209	with some fixed positive exponents, the contribution
   210	$m^2 (md/q)^{c}$ is not dominated by any vanishing function of $m^2\eps$
   211	and $md/q$, as the scaling $\eps = 0$, $md/q = m^{-2/c}$ shows, and the
   212	$\eps$-contribution fails similarly for sublinear exponents.  Neither
   213	observation asserts that the \emph{conclusion} of the lemma is false for
   214	some error function of the claimed form; the defect is that the printed
   215	proof does not deliver it.
   216	
   217	For orientation, the algebraic identity
   218	$m\,\eps^{1/2} = (m^2\eps)^{1/2}$ shows what a derivation of the claimed
   219	$\eps$-dependence would need: a chain that loses only square roots in the
   220	$\eps$-type quantities \emph{after} the restricted-distribution
   221	inflation would produce terms of the shape $(m^2\eps)^{1/2}$.  The
   222	printed chain loses fourth roots, through two nested Cauchy--Schwarz
   223	steps applied to already square-rooted quantities, and its
   224	$md/q$-dependence enters as $m\,\delta_P^{1/4}$, which the claimed form
   225	cannot absorb.
   226	
   227	\section{Correction and alternative repairs}
   228	
   229	The first direction below is the one the blueprint adopts; the remaining
   230	directions are alternatives, none of which is claimed as established.
   231	
   232	\paragraph{Corrected error form (adopted in the proof).}
   233	The operative error form is
   234	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$ --- concretely,
   235	the first-route bound.  Following the proof-gap protocol, the source-labelled
   236	statement keeps its printed form and the correction is carried by the proof,
   237	by the chapter remark, and by a separate formalization-support node, rather
   238	than being substituted silently into the source statement.  The only consumer
   239	is the polynomial-pair lemma, whose imported error
   240	$a(md)^a(\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ absorbs
   241	$m^{O(1)}$ prefactors by enlarging $a$ and shrinking $b$.  The blueprint proof
   242	records this absorption and the corrected deficit reading of the second claim.
   243	Two obligations remain: carry out that absorption with explicit constants when
   244	the lemma is formalized, and prove the three chained estimates.
   245	
   246	\paragraph{Repairing the second route.}
   247	Strengthen Property~2 of the sub-line lemma to the joint product law: in
   248	each mixture component, the pairs $(\ell_X, x)$ and $(\ell_Z, z)$ are
   249	independent with the stated restricted-distribution laws.  The sampling
   250	procedure makes this plausible, since in each component the two pairs
   251	are built from disjoint collections of the independent ingredients (the
   252	two blocks of the uniform point, the direction blocks, and the fresh
   253	auxiliary choices).  Open obligations: (i)~state and prove the
   254	strengthened property for every component, including lines whose
   255	direction blocks vanish and degenerate to singletons; (ii)~re-derive the
   256	mixture decomposition of $\Lambda$ from the strengthened property;
   257	(iii)~note that even then the route delivers only
   258	$O(m^2\delta_P) = m^2 \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$, so this direction removes
   259	the unsupported step of the printed proof but still requires the
   260	error-form decision of the previous direction, with $m^2$ in place of
   261	$m$.
   262	
   263	\paragraph{Establishing the claimed form.}
   264	Re-derive the chain so that every factor of $m$ enters jointly with
   265	$\eps$ as $m^2\eps$, in the sense of the orientation identity above.
   266	Open obligations: (i)~find a chaining that avoids one of the two nested
   267	square-root losses, or prove restricted-distribution versions of the
   268	underlying consistency lemmas directly at their inflated errors;
   269	(ii)~handle the $md/q$-dependence, since a residual term
   270	$m (md/q)^{c}$ is incompatible with the claimed form for the current
   271	exponents.  No derivation along these lines is known here, and the
   272	direction may be infeasible; in that case the corrected error form of
   273	the first direction stands.
   274	
   275	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   276	
   277	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} keeps the combined-lines lemma in
   278	its source shape, error form $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$ included, and marks in
   279	the proof that this form remains unproved: the proof derives the first route
   280	only, records the established bound $m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$, and uses
   281	that bound in the sequel.  The
   282	three claims are stated as separate lemmas with the corrected deficit
   283	assertion for the second; the sub-line lemma states Property~2 at the
   284	level of the two marginal laws and expressly disclaims the joint
   285	conditional law of the two points, so the blueprint statement does not
   286	license the second route; and the polynomial-pair lemma's proof absorbs
   287	the $m$ prefactor into the constants of the imported soundness error.  A
   288	chapter remark summarizes the discrepancy and cites this note.%
   289	\footnote{The blueprint statements are \path{lem:qld-4-13},
   290	\path{lem:qld-sublines}, \path{lem:claim-17-1}--\path{lem:claim-17-3},
   291	\path{lem:qld-4-7}, and the remark
   292	\path{rem:qld-4-13-source-defects}, all in
   293	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}.}
   294	
   295	The source-labelled lemma links the carrier
   296	\path{ExtendedLinesWitness} and the declaration
   297	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness}, which retains the printed error form
   298	$\poly(m^2\eps,md/q)$ and whose proof is the tracked obligation.  The
   299	established error form is linked from the separate formalization-support node
   300	\path{lem:qld-4-13-established}, whose declaration
   301	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_established} has the explicit form
   302	$C m\,\poly(\eps,md/q)$ for a universal $C>0$; this agrees with the blueprint
   303	convention that constants are absorbed into $\poly$.  Both proofs are open.
   304	
   305	Neither declaration is source-shaped beyond its error form, and this note does
   306	not claim otherwise.  Both return the carrier \path{ExtendedLinesWitness},
   307	which replaces the source's lines in $\F_q^{2m+2}$ by the directly indexed
   308	extended line space of
   309	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}, averages over the
   310	corresponding directly indexed line-point law instead of over the line-point
   311	distribution instantiated at dimension $2m+2$, and compares both sides of its
   312	two consistency displays on the completed answer alphabet
   313	$\F_q\cup\{\bot\}$, whose extra outcome collects the line polynomials that
   314	admit no evaluation at the sampled point, in place of the source's answer
   315	summation over $a\in\F_q$.  Neither blueprint node therefore carries a
   316	statement-level formalization mark, and relating the two formulations is the
   317	transport obligation of that note.
   318	
   319	\section{Conclusion}
   320	
   321	There is a proof-level gap in the cited lemma, together with an
   322	intermediate inconsistency: the printed proof asserts two different
   323	bounds for the same consistency defect, the first-route bound
   324	$O(m(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4} +
   325	\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}))$ and the second-route bound
   326	$O(m^2\delta_P)$, the second resting on a joint-law decomposition that
   327	the sub-line lemma as stated does not supply; and the error form claimed
   328	in the lemma statement, $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, follows from neither.
   329	The first route is sound after a harmless deficit correction in its
   330	second claim and establishes $m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$.  The
   331	discrepancy is harmless downstream, since the sole consumer absorbs
   332	polynomial-in-$m$ prefactors into its constants.  The blueprint therefore
   333	retains the printed statement with the missing step explicitly tracked, uses
   334	the corrected first-route form in the proof and in the sequel, and cites this
   335	note; strengthening the sub-line lemma to license the second route is
   336	optional, and no route to the printed form is currently known.  We do not
   337	assert that the printed form is false.

    59	\section{Key theorem forms}
    60	
    61	Throughout, $q = 2^k$ with $k$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple
    62	$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \ge 1$ and $m \mid q$, and
    63	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
    64	over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four
    65	theorem forms.
    66	\begin{enumerate}
    67	  \item \textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There
    68	  is a function $\delta_S(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,
    69	  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every
    70	  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test
    71	  succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, there is a projective
    72	  measurement $\{\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in
    73	  $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\delta_S$-consistent, on
    74	  average over a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$ and in both bases
    75	  $W \in \{X,Z\}$, with the corresponding points measurements
    76	  $\{\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$ of the strategy, together with the
    77	  symmetric counterpart of this relation.
    78	  \item \textbf{Missing instantiation obligation.}  The classical low
    79	  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)$ is well
    80	  defined, and the combined point and line measurements assembled in the
    81	  analysis constitute a strategy for it of value at least
    82	  $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$.  The game's question distribution draws
    83	  its axis and diagonal indices through an index function
    84	  $\chi_{2m+2}\colon \F_q \to \{1,\ldots,2m+2\}$ with classes of equal size
    85	  $q/(2m+2)$, so the game exists only when $2m+2$ divides $q$.
    86	  \item \textbf{Restricted form supported by the present route.}  The source
    87	  theorem form under the additional hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$.  Among
    88	  admissible tuples this hypothesis holds exactly when $m = 1$ and
    89	  $q \ge 8$; it fails for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ and for

   108	\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}
   109	
   110	We examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical
   111	low-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression
   112	paper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,
   113	arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
   114	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
   115	\footnote{Tracked in \localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source
   116	consulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at
   117	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   118	lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
   119	line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization
   120	with its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its
   121	proof, and admissibility are at
   122	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   123	lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}
   124	There, the combined point measurements
   125	$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
   126	$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
   127	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
   128	individual degree game with parameters
   129	\[
   130	  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
   131	  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
   132	\]
   133	of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
   134	for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
   135	The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution
   136	over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
   137	
   138	The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
   139	admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
   140	incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
   141	in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
   142	$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
   143	$\chi(s)$ with
   144	\[
   145	  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
   146	  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
   147	\]
   148	so that the $m'$ classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\F_q$ into sets of equal
   149	size $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \nmid q$ neither the index
   150	function nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.
   151	
   152	Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
   153	is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
   154	$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
   155	divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
   156	admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is
   157	undefined for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$: for instance
   158	$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs
   159	the instantiation without addressing the divisibility, so its proof route
   160	establishes the polynomial-pair lemma, and with it the soundness theorem for
   161	the Pauli basis test that rests on it, only for $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.
   162	
   163	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   164	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   165	
   166	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   167	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   168	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   169	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   170	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   171	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   172	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   173	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   174	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   175	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
   176	the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
   177	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   178	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
   179	open.  Both obligations are independent of the divisibility question: they
   180	arise at every dimension, for the $\chi$-based game where it is defined and
   181	equally for the directly indexed variant proposed under the candidate
   182	repairs.
   183	
   184	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   185	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   186	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
   187	measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
   188	three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
   189	subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
   190	test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
   191	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
   192	direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
   193	send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
   194	$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
   195	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
   196	last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly
   197	in $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to
   198	one prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to
   199	the other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \emph{Synchronicity
   200	test}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered
   201	pair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their
   202	answers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this
   203	test with probability $1-\eps$ together with an integer parameter
   204	$K \ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code
   205	--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and
   206	distance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements
   207	$\{G_c\}$ and $\{\tilde G_c\}$ with outcomes in $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$,
   208	consistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's
   209	lines measurements, and with each other, up to
   210	$\eta'(m',t,K,\eps,n^{-1}) = \mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \cdot
   211	\mathrm{poly}(\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.
   212	
   213	\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}
   214	The source asserts that the $\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$
   215	is this test.  It is not, in four respects.
   216	(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals
   217	two points of a \emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent
   218	--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line
   219	question reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$
   220	polynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the
   221	diagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$
   222	and $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and
   223	both directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line
   224	description carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of
   225	the pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the
   226	compatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the
   227	\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the
   228	\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The
   229	construction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the
   230	hidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.
   231	(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \in \F_q$; the test's
   232	carry only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class
   233	$\chi^{-1}(i)$, and removing this dependence runs into the fiber-averaging
   234	difficulty made explicit under the candidate repairs: averaging preserves
   235	the line-versus-point branches exactly but not the synchronicity branches.
   236	(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$
   237	in the test against $2/9$ in the game.  Once the per-branch predicates are
   238	matched, the intended bookkeeping bound is that the constructed strategy's
   239	rejection probability in the test is at most $\tfrac32$ times the game's
   240	rejection probability, up to the $O(1/(m'q))$ of item~(iv); this bound is
   241	the target of the obligation, not an established fact.
   242	(iv)~The game's predicate fixes an acceptance convention on diagonal
   243	questions with zero direction --- an event of probability at most
   244	$2/(m'q)$, recorded in the blueprint's remark on zero directions --- for
   245	which the test has no counterpart branch.
   246	Finally, the displayed conclusions of Theorem~4.7 pair one prover's points
   247	measurements with the other prover's tensor-codeword measurement, and the
   248	first prover's tensor-codeword measurement with the second prover's lines
   249	measurements, while the game-level statement asserts the point consistency
   250	in both directions; deriving the stated form uses the role symmetrization
   251	of the test and belongs to the correspondence.  None of these steps is
   252	difficult to state, but none is carried out in the source, and together
   253	they replace the asserted one-line identity by a reduction carrying its
   254	own value bound.
   255	
   256	\paragraph{Obligation 2: the parameter bound.}
   257	Theorem~4.7 requires $K \ge 12 m' t = 12 m' (d+1)$.  The source
   258	instantiates $K = (m')^3 d$, which meets the bound iff
   259	$(m')^2 d \ge 12(d+1)$: this holds for all $d \ge 1$ when $m' \ge 5$,
   260	holds at $m' = 4$ exactly when $d \ge 3$, and fails for every $d$ when
   261	$m' \le 3$.  In the game's parameter domain the dimension divides the
   262	admissible field size and is therefore a power of two, so the source's
   263	instantiation violates the hypothesis exactly at $m' \in \{1,2\}$ for
   264	every $d$ and at $m' = 4$ for $d \in \{1,2\}$ --- in particular, in the
   265	multilinear regime $d = 1$, at every dimension $m' \le 4$.  A candidate
   266	repair is to instantiate $K = \max((m')^3 d,\, 12 m'(d+1))$; the open
   267	obligation is then to re-absorb the error, that is, to check that
   268	$\mathrm{poly}(m',t,K)$ and $e^{-K/(m')^2}$ still collapse to the form
   269	$a(dm')^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bm'd})$ in the small-$m'$ cases where the
   270	maximum is $12m'(d+1)$ --- plausible, since there
   271	$e^{-K/(m')^2} = e^{-12(d+1)/m'}$ decays in $d$ at a rate comparable to
   272	$2^{-m'd}$ for $m' \le 4$, but not checked here.
   273	
   274	In the correspondence of Obligation~1, the only role of the divisibility
   275	$m' \mid q$ is to make the $\chi$-sampled index uniform.  The underlying
   276	mathematics does not need the divisibility.  The low
   277	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} samples its axis
   278	index $i$ uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly, with no index function
   279	on $\F_q$ and no divisibility hypothesis,%
   280	\footnote{See the test figure in \path{references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex}.}
   281	and the tensor-code test is likewise a test about the code
   282	$\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$, not about an encoding of indices into $\F_q$.  The
   283	$\chi$-based packaging exists so that the question distribution is
   284	conditionally linear, which the introspection machinery requires for the
   285	game the players actually play --- the Pauli basis test at dimension $m$,
   286	where admissibility does supply the divisibility.  The game at dimension
   287	$2m+2$ never appears in a verifier; it is an internal analysis device in the
   288	proof of the polynomial-pair lemma, so nothing there requires its question

   292	
   293	\paragraph{Direct index sampling (candidate direction, recommended).}
   294	Define, for arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the line-point distribution over
   295	$\F_q^{m'}$ that samples the uniform point, the uniform axis index
   296	$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
   297	$i-1$ coordinates, directly; define the \emph{directly indexed game} with
   298	this question distribution, whose line questions carry the index $i$ (and,
   299	for diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place of the seed
   300	$s \in \F_q$; and state the imported soundness theorem for that game
   301	(form~4 above).  This removes the divisibility obstruction and nothing
   302	else: the directly indexed game still asks for polynomials on revealed
   303	lines, has no pair questions, and weighs its branches as the present game
   304	does, so establishing form~4 carries the same two import obligations as
   305	the $\chi$-based import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), now at
   306	arbitrary dimension.
   307	
   308	The relation to the present game when $m' \mid q$ must moreover be proved
   309	at the level of games, not merely of question distributions, because the
   310	two games have different question alphabets: an $\mathsf{ALine}$ question
   311	of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0, s)$ and a $\mathsf{DLine}$
   312	question a triple $(u_0, s, v')$, so a strategy may select different
   313	measurements for seeds $s \ne s'$ with $\chi(s) = \chi(s')$, and equality
   314	of the induced laws of the geometric data does not by itself transport
   315	such a strategy.  The transport layer decomposes into the following
   316	obligations, none of which is carried out here.
   317	\begin{itemize}
   318	  \item \emph{Distribution lemma.}  When $m' \mid q$, the image of the
   319	  conditionally linear question distribution under the parsing map
   320	  $(u_0,s) \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s))$, $(u_0,s,v') \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s),v')$
   321	  is the direct distribution, and conditioned on the parsed question the
   322	  seed is uniform on the class $\chi^{-1}(i)$, independently of everything
   323	  else.
   324	  \item \emph{Parsing pullback.}  A strategy for the directly indexed game
   325	  composed with the parsing map is a seed-oblivious strategy for the
   326	  $\chi$-based game.  Since the win predicate depends on the question only
   327	  through the parsed data, and a seed-oblivious strategy answers
   328	  identically across each fiber --- in particular on the synchronicity
   329	  branches, where both players hold the same seed --- the value should be
   330	  preserved exactly on every branch, and projectivity is preserved.  This
   331	  is the direction the combining subtree needs.
   332	  \item \emph{Seed-fiber averaging: what it preserves and what it does
   333	  not.}  In the opposite direction, average each line measurement over its
   334	  seed fiber: attach to a direct question $(u_0,i)$, respectively
   335	  $(u_0,i,v')$, the average over uniform $s \in \chi^{-1}(i)$ of the
   336	  measurements attached to $(u_0,s)$, respectively $(u_0,s,v')$, leaving
   337	  the points measurements unchanged.  By the conditional uniformity of the
   338	  seed this preserves the value of every \emph{line-versus-point} branch
   339	  exactly: there the paired question carries no seed, so the branch value
   340	  is an average over the fiber of per-seed values, which the averaged
   341	  measurement computes.  It does \emph{not} preserve the synchronicity
   342	  branches.  There both players hold the same seed, so the $\chi$-based
   343	  branch value is the diagonal average
   344	  $\E_{s}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s)}_f
   345	  \rangle$, while the averaged strategy realizes the double average
   346	  $\E_{s,s'}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s')}_f
   347	  \rangle$ over independent seeds in the fiber; the two differ whenever
   348	  the players' measurements vary across a fiber in a correlated way (if
   349	  both apply a common seed-dependent relabelling, every diagonal term is
   350	  large and the cross terms are not), and neither quantity dominates the
   351	  other in general.  An earlier revision of this note claimed that the
   352	  averaging preserves the exact value, and with it synchronicity; that
   353	  claim was wrong and is withdrawn.  What needs proof is control of the
   354	  synchronicity branches under de-seeding.  Candidate approaches: show
   355	  that a strategy of value $1-\eps$ in the $\chi$-based game is, with
   356	  polynomial loss, close to a seed-oblivious one; or state form~4 with a
   357	  synchronicity hypothesis in the doubled-average form and re-derive it on
   358	  the tensor-code side.  Choosing and proving one of these is an open
   359	  obligation.
   360	  \item \emph{Projectivity round trip.}  The averaged strategy is a POVM
   361	  strategy even when the given one is projective, while the imported
   362	  theorem, like the present one, takes projective strategies.  The
   363	  intended round trip is: dilate the averaged strategy to a projective one
   364	  (Naimark preserves all product correlations
   365	  $\langle X \ot Y \rangle$ of the given strategy against the dilated
   366	  state --- hence the value of every branch the averaging preserved ---
   367	  but nothing restores the diagonal seed correlations once the averaging
   368	  has been performed); apply form~4; and compress the resulting polynomial
   369	  measurement along the dilation isometry back to a POVM in the required
   370	  measurement class on the original space.  That this compression
   371	  preserves the consistency conclusions must itself be proved; it is
   372	  stated here as an obligation, not established.  (Alternatively, form~4
   373	  may be stated for POVM strategies outright, moving the dilation inside
   374	  the import.)
   375	\end{itemize}

    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}

    32	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} The inequality
