   163	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   164	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   165	
   166	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   167	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   168	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   169	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   170	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   171	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   172	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   173	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   174	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   175	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
   176	the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
   177	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   178	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
   179	open.  Both obligations are independent of the divisibility question: they
   180	arise at every dimension, for the $\chi$-based game where it is defined and
   181	equally for the directly indexed variant proposed under the candidate
   182	repairs.
   183	
   184	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   185	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   186	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
   187	measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
   188	three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
   189	subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
   190	test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
   191	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
   192	direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
   193	send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
   194	$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
   195	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
   196	last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly
   197	in $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to
   198	one prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to
   199	the other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \emph{Synchronicity
   200	test}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered
   201	pair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their
   202	answers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this
   203	test with probability $1-\eps$ together with an integer parameter
   204	$K \ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code
   205	--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and
   206	distance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements
   207	$\{G_c\}$ and $\{\tilde G_c\}$ with outcomes in $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$,
   208	consistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's
   209	lines measurements, and with each other, up to
   210	$\eta'(m',t,K,\eps,n^{-1}) = \mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \cdot
   211	\mathrm{poly}(\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.
   212	
   213	\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}
   214	The source asserts that the $\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$
   215	is this test.  It is not, in four respects.
   216	(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals
   217	two points of a \emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent
   218	--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line
   219	question reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$
   220	polynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the
   221	diagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$
   222	and $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and
   223	both directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line
   224	description carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of
   225	the pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the
   226	compatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the
   227	\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the
   228	\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The
   229	construction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the
   230	hidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.
   231	(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \in \F_q$; the test's
   232	carry only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class
   233	$\chi^{-1}(i)$, and removing this dependence runs into the fiber-averaging
   234	difficulty made explicit under the candidate repairs: averaging preserves
   235	the line-versus-point branches exactly but not the synchronicity branches.
   236	(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$
   237	in the test against $2/9$ in the game.  Once the per-branch predicates are
   238	matched, the intended bookkeeping bound is that the constructed strategy's
   239	rejection probability in the test is at most $\tfrac32$ times the game's
   240	rejection probability, up to the $O(1/(m'q))$ of item~(iv); this bound is
   241	the target of the obligation, not an established fact.
   242	(iv)~The game's predicate fixes an acceptance convention on diagonal
   243	questions with zero direction --- an event of probability at most
   244	$2/(m'q)$, recorded in the blueprint's remark on zero directions --- for
   245	which the test has no counterpart branch.
   246	Finally, the displayed conclusions of Theorem~4.7 pair one prover's points
   247	measurements with the other prover's tensor-codeword measurement, and the
   248	first prover's tensor-codeword measurement with the second prover's lines
   249	measurements, while the game-level statement asserts the point consistency
   250	in both directions; deriving the stated form uses the role symmetrization
   251	of the test and belongs to the correspondence.  None of these steps is
   252	difficult to state, but none is carried out in the source, and together
   253	they replace the asserted one-line identity by a reduction carrying its
   254	own value bound.
   255	
   256	\paragraph{Obligation 2: the parameter bound.}
   257	Theorem~4.7 requires $K \ge 12 m' t = 12 m' (d+1)$.  The source
   258	instantiates $K = (m')^3 d$, which meets the bound iff
   259	$(m')^2 d \ge 12(d+1)$: this holds for all $d \ge 1$ when $m' \ge 5$,
   260	holds at $m' = 4$ exactly when $d \ge 3$, and fails for every $d$ when
   261	$m' \le 3$.  In the game's parameter domain the dimension divides the
   262	admissible field size and is therefore a power of two, so the source's
   263	instantiation violates the hypothesis exactly at $m' \in \{1,2\}$ for
   264	every $d$ and at $m' = 4$ for $d \in \{1,2\}$ --- in particular, in the
   265	multilinear regime $d = 1$, at every dimension $m' \le 4$.  A candidate
   266	repair is to instantiate $K = \max((m')^3 d,\, 12 m'(d+1))$; the open
   267	obligation is then to re-absorb the error, that is, to check that
   268	$\mathrm{poly}(m',t,K)$ and $e^{-K/(m')^2}$ still collapse to the form
   269	$a(dm')^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bm'd})$ in the small-$m'$ cases where the
   270	maximum is $12m'(d+1)$ --- plausible, since there
   271	$e^{-K/(m')^2} = e^{-12(d+1)/m'}$ decays in $d$ at a rate comparable to
   272	$2^{-m'd}$ for $m' \le 4$, but not checked here.
   273	
   274	In the correspondence of Obligation~1, the only role of the divisibility
   275	$m' \mid q$ is to make the $\chi$-sampled index uniform.  The underlying
   276	mathematics does not need the divisibility.  The low
   277	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} samples its axis
   278	index $i$ uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly, with no index function
   279	on $\F_q$ and no divisibility hypothesis,%
   280	\footnote{See the test figure in \path{references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex}.}
   281	and the tensor-code test is likewise a test about the code
   282	$\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$, not about an encoding of indices into $\F_q$.  The
   283	$\chi$-based packaging exists so that the question distribution is
   284	conditionally linear, which the introspection machinery requires for the
   285	game the players actually play --- the Pauli basis test at dimension $m$,
   286	where admissibility does supply the divisibility.  The game at dimension
   287	$2m+2$ never appears in a verifier; it is an internal analysis device in the
   288	proof of the polynomial-pair lemma, so nothing there requires its question
   289	distribution to be conditionally linear.

     3	/-!
     4	# Combining the point measurements
     5	
     6	This module states the construction obligation for the joint X/Z point
     7	measurements and defines their scalar linear coarse-graining.  The latter is

    29	/-- A pair of source points and the two scalar coefficients used by the
    30	extended point measurement. -/
    31	abbrev ExtendedPointQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    32	  ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) ×
    33	    (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P)
    34	
    35	namespace CombinedPointsWitness
    36	
    37	/-- Coarse-grain a joint point measurement by `(a,b) |-> alpha*a + beta*b`
    38	on the selected player side.  This is the concrete measurement of
    39	`lem:qld-4-12`, paper lines 993--1011. -/
    40	noncomputable def extendedQ {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δ : ℝ}
    41	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε} (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δ)
    42	    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)
    43	    (alpha beta : PauliScalar P) :
    44	    Measurement (PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
    45	  (points.Q side x z).postprocess fun ab => alpha * ab.1 + beta * ab.2
    46	
    47	end CombinedPointsWitness
    48	
    49	/-- Construction of the projective joint point measurements of
    50	`lem:qld-4-10`, paper lines 689--709.  The witness retains both ordered
    51	products and all four directed heterogeneous placement comparisons. -/
    52	theorem exists_combinedPointsWitness :
    53	    ∃ deltaQ : ℝ -> ℝ, IsPolyErr deltaQ ∧
    54	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε),
    55	        Nonempty (CombinedPointsWitness S (deltaQ ε)) := by
    56	  sorry
    57

    59	`CombinedPointsWitness.extendedQ`.  This is `lem:qld-4-12`, paper lines
    60	993--1011; the `XZ` and `ZX` source products remain separate. -/
    61	theorem extendedQ_spec {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δ : ℝ}
    62	    {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε} (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δ) :
    63	    (∀ side x z alpha beta,
    64	      Measurement.IsProjective (points.extendedQ side x z alpha beta)) ∧
    65	    (∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
    66	      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (ExtendedPointQuestion P))
    67	        (fun question c => S.place p1
    68	          ((points.extendedQ p1.side question.1.1 question.1.2
    69	            question.2.1 question.2.2).effect c))
    70	        (fun question c => S.place p2
    71	          ((points.extendedQ p2.side question.1.1 question.1.2
    72	            question.2.1 question.2.2).effect c))
    73	        S.psiHat <= δ) ∧
    74	    (∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
    75	      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (ExtendedPointQuestion P))
    76	        (fun question c => S.place p1
    77	          ((points.extendedQ p1.side question.1.1 question.1.2
    78	            question.2.1 question.2.2).effect c))
    79	        (fun question c => S.place p2
    80	          (∑ ab ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P =>
    81	              question.2.1 * ab.1 + question.2.2 * ab.2 = c),
    82	            (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X question.1.1).effect ab.1 *
    83	              (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z question.1.2).effect ab.2))
    84	        S.psiHat <= δ) ∧
    85	    ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
    86	      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (ExtendedPointQuestion P))
    87	        (fun question c => S.place p1
    88	          ((points.extendedQ p1.side question.1.1 question.1.2
    89	            question.2.1 question.2.2).effect c))
    90	        (fun question c => S.place p2
    91	          (∑ ab ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P =>
    92	              question.2.1 * ab.1 + question.2.2 * ab.2 = c),
    93	            (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z question.1.2).effect ab.2 *
    94	              (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X question.1.1).effect ab.1))
    95	        S.psiHat <= δ := by

    23	  incorrect numerical steps and later suppresses the range projection when
    24	  passing from unitary conjugation to isometry conjugation.
    25	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} A corrected positive-contraction estimate,
    26	  a small-error case split for normalization, and one range-projection transfer
    27	  lemma for a projective measurement family.
    28	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Positivity, contraction inequalities,
    29	  isometry range projections, and norm estimates belong to finite-dimensional
    30	  Hilbert-space algebra.  The state-dependent family distance and register
    31	  placements are project-local.
    32	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} The inequality
    33	  $H^2\geq2H-I$ for a positive contraction, the triangle inequality, and
    34	  $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$ for an isometry.  The repair is tracked in
    35	  \ghissue{19}.
    36	\end{itemize}
    37	
    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    41	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    42	\[
    43	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    44	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    45	\]
    46	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    47	\[
    48	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    49	  \qquad
    50	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    51	\]
    52	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    53	\[
    54	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    55	\]
    56	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    57	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    58	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    59	
    60	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    61	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    62	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    63	\[
    64	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    65	\]
    66	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    67	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    68	$\Delta$.
    69	
    70	\section{Numerical defects in the source proof}
    71	
    72	Lines~1715--1742 of
    73	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    74	construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
    75	estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
    76	$\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
    77	source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
    78	\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
    79	small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
    80	$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
    81	
    82	The triangle inequality yields
    83	\[
    84	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
    85	\]
    86	so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
    87	$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
    88	$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
    89	universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
    90	vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
    91	are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.
    92	
    93	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    94	
    95	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    96	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    97	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
    98	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
    99	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   100	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   101	
   102	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   103	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   104	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   105	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   106	\[
   107	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   108	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   109	\]
   110	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   111	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   112	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   113	
   114	This transfer is an open proof obligation for the next extraction stage.  It
   115	must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
   116	estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,
   117	residual assumption, or hypothesis of the source-labelled soundness theorem.
   118	
   119	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   120	
   121	The proof of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} and the soundness proof in
   122	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} use the corrected
   123	positive-contraction estimate, make the small-error case distinction explicit,
   124	and isolate the range-projection calculation.  The chapter therefore preserves
   125	the source's state and observable conclusions while exposing the omitted
   126	argument.
   127	
   128	The structure \path{ExtractionWitness} in
   129	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Unitary.lean} contains only the two-sided
   130	unitarity equations for the concrete swap maps, a normalized auxiliary state,
   131	the transformed-state estimate, and the two-player Pauli-projector comparison.
   132	The theorem \path{exists_extractionWitness_ofGlobalPairWitness} concludes the
   133	existence of this data at the explicit extraction scale, but it takes the
   134	\path{GlobalPairWitness} of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-4-7} as an explicit hypothesis
   135	rather than obtaining it from \path{exists_globalPairWitness}.  That bundle
   136	carries the projective global polynomial-pair measurements and both
   137	point-consistency estimates, and the blueprint proof of
   138	Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} obtains it from Lemma~\path{lem:qld-4-7}; deleting
   139	the hypothesis would leave that construction unproved.  By the criterion of
   140	\path{docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex} the hypothesis is therefore proof
   141	debt rather than a faithful boundary condition, and the declaration is a
   142	conditional helper: it does not certify the source lemma, and the blueprint
   143	node Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} accordingly neither links it nor carries any
   144	statement-level formalization mark.  The declaration is recorded instead on the
   145	separate formalization-support node
   146	\path{lem:qld-unitary-given-global-pair}, whose statement assumes the global
   147	polynomial-pair measurement explicitly and whose formal link points only to the
   148	conditional helper.  It therefore cannot be mistaken for the source result.
   149	Apart from that hypothesis the
   150	conclusion matches the Stage~4.2 extraction lemma, including the corrected
   151	numerical estimates; the later passage to the isometries in the soundness
   152	theorem is not formalized, and no declaration yet states that passage.
   153	
   154	The misleading source-facing description has been removed.  The suffix
   155	\path{ofGlobalPairWitness} now quarantines the extra premise in the helper's
   156	name, and its docstring explicitly identifies the result as conditional and
   157	marks its dependence on the witness as unfaithful.  Discharging the debt still
   158	requires composing \path{exists_globalPairWitness} with this helper to obtain
   159	the source lemma; no declaration currently carries out that composition.
   160	
   161	Issue~\#19 owns this concrete Stage~4.2 interface and discrepancy record.
   162	\ghissue{123} owns the source-facing composition through
   163	\path{exists_globalPairWitness}.  \ghissue{47} tracks the separate
   164	range-projection transfer needed by \path{pauli_soundness}; that theorem must
   165	be derived from the concrete data rather than stored in the witness.
   166	
   167	\section{Conclusion}
   168	
   169	The printed triangle calculation has repairable numerical errors, and the
   170	last passage from unitaries to isometries omits a genuine range-projection
   171	argument.  Neither defect is a counterexample to Pauli soundness.  The former
   172	is corrected by positive-contraction inequalities and a small-error split;
   173	the latter remains a named downstream proof obligation whose hypotheses are
   174	already supplied by the extraction lemma.  Independently of both defects, the
   175	present extraction declaration is conditional on the global polynomial-pair
   176	measurement, and that conditionality must be removed before it may be
   177	advertised as the source lemma.

    27	/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the
    28	direct scalar field. -/
    29	abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=
    30	  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D
    31	
    32	/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
    33	and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
    34	keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
    35	def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)
    36	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    37	    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
    38	  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    39	    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →
    40	      evalCoefficient f t = a
    41	
    42	/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an
    43	explicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field
    44	value is used as a fallback. -/
    45	noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    46	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    47	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by
    48	  classical
    49	  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    50	    some (Classical.choose h)
    51	  else none

    54	abbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D

    57	coordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and

    59	noncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :
    60	    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D
    61	  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩
    62	  | .aline, sample =>
    63	      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
    64	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩
    65	  | .dline, sample =>
    66	      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
    67	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩

    72	noncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :
    73	    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=
    74	  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    75	    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),
    76	      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))
    77	
    78	/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/
    79	theorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
    80	    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by
    81	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability
    82	    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _
    83	
    84	/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    85	inductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where
    86	  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)
    87	  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    88	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    89	  deriving DecidableEq
    90	
    91	/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/
    92	abbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=
    93	  (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    94	    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    95	      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D))
    96	
    97	/-- Constructor-preserving equivalence between the inductive answer type and
    98	its finite code. -/
    99	noncomputable def directLdAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   100	    DirectLdAnswer D ≃ DirectLdAnswerCode D where
   101	  toFun
   102	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   103	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   104	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   105	  invFun
   106	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   107	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   108	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   109	  left_inv := by intro answer; cases answer <;> rfl
   110	  right_inv := by
   111	    intro answer
   112	    rcases answer with a | a
   113	    · rfl
   114	    · rcases a with a | a <;> rfl
   115	
   116	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Inhabited (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   117	  ⟨.pointVals 0⟩
   118	
   119	noncomputable instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Fintype (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   120	  Fintype.ofEquiv (DirectLdAnswerCode D) (directLdAnswerEquiv D).symm
   121	
   122	/-- Check that a direct-game answer has the constructor required by its
   123	question type. -/
   124	def validDirectLdAnswer {D : DirectLdParams} (t : LdType)
   125	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) : Bool :=
   126	  match t, answer with
   127	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   128	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   129	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   130	  | _, _ => false
   131	
   132	/-- The directly indexed axis-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   133	def directAlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   134	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   135	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   136	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   137	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   138	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection line.index →
   139	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   140	
   141	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   142	def directDlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   143	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   144	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   145	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   146	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   147	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   148	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   149	
   150	/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from
   151	`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line
   152	question. -/
   153	noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :
   154	    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →
   155	      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
   156	  open Classical in
   157	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   158	    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
   159	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   160	      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   161	      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   162	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   163	      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   164	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   165	      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   166	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   167	      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   168	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   169	      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   170	      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   171	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   172	    else false
   173	
   174	/-- The directly indexed low-degree game at an arbitrary positive dimension.
   175	It is an internal analysis game, not the conditionally linear verifier game
   176	`ldGame`. -/
   177	noncomputable def directLdGame (D : DirectLdParams) : Game where
   178	  QuestionA := DirectLdQuestion D
   179	  QuestionB := DirectLdQuestion D
   180	  AnswerA := DirectLdAnswer D
   181	  AnswerB := DirectLdAnswer D
   182	  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D
   183	  μ_prob := directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D
   184	  decide := directLdWinPredicate D
   185	
   186	/-- The canonical point question associated with a geometric point. -/
   187	def directLdPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   188	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   189	  (.point, ⟨u, D.firstIndex, 0⟩)
   190	
   191	/-- Total point-answer relabeling used in the direct soundness conclusion.
   192	Wrong-form answers are folded into the zero tuple, exactly as for
   193	`ldPointValuesOrZero`. -/
   194	def directLdPointValuesOrZero (D : DirectLdParams) :
   195	    DirectLdAnswer D → Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D
   196	  | .pointVals values => values
   197	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   198	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   199	
   200	/-- A simultaneous tuple of bounded polynomials for the directly indexed
   201	game. -/
   202	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyTuple (D : DirectLdParams) :=
   203	  Fin D.k → PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d
   204	
   205	/-- A polynomial-tuple POVM for the directly indexed game. -/
   206	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyMeasTuple (D : DirectLdParams) (ι : Type*)
   207	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   208	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectPolyTuple D) ι
   209	
   210	/-- Evaluate every component of a direct polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   211	def evalDirectPolyTupleAt {D : DirectLdParams}
   212	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :
   213	    Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D :=
   214	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   215	
   216	end
   217

     4	# Soundness for the directly indexed low-degree game
     5	
     6	This module isolates the quantum soundness obligation for the directly indexed
     7	low-degree game.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The obligation supports the Chapter 15 combining argument at
    12	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1267-1288`.
    13	-/
    14	
    15	open scoped BigOperators
    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    20	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    21	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    22	
    23	noncomputable section
    24	
    25	/-- Quantum soundness obligation for the directly indexed low-degree game.
    26	This is the repaired import form proposed in
    27	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, needed by the Chapter 15
    28	combining argument at paper
    29	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1267-1288`.
    30	
    31	This is a formalization auxiliary assertion, not the source-labelled
    32	`lem:ld-soundness`.  Its proof must establish the game-correspondence and
    33	auxiliary-parameter bounds catalogued in the cited gap note; neither is hidden
    34	as a hypothesis here. -/
    35	theorem exists_direct_ld_soundness :
    36	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
    37	      ∀ (D : DirectLdParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
    38	        ∀ S : Strategy (directLdGame D), S.IsProjective → 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
    39	          ∃ GA : DirectPolyMeasTuple D S.ιA,
    40	            ∃ GB : DirectPolyMeasTuple D S.ιB,
    41	              consistencyDefect
    42	                  (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
    43	                  (fun u outcome =>
    44	                    heteroKron
    45	                      (((S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
    46	                        (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect outcome) 1)
    47	                  (fun u outcome =>
    48	                    heteroKron 1
    49	                      ((GB.postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
    50	                  S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε D.q D.m D.d D.k ∧
    51	              consistencyDefect
    52	                  (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
    53	                  (fun u outcome =>
    54	                    heteroKron
    55	                      ((GA.postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
    56	                  (fun u outcome =>
    57	                    heteroKron 1
    58	                      (((S.B (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
    59	                        (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect outcome))
    60	                  S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε D.q D.m D.d D.k ∧
    61	              consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
    62	                  (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
    63	                  (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
    64	                  S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε D.q D.m D.d D.k := by
    65	  sorry
    66	
    67	end

   182	/-- Coefficient evaluation agrees with evaluation of the corresponding mature
   183	diagonal-line polynomial. -/
   184	theorem directDiagonalAnswerEquiv_apply (D : DirectLdParams)
   185	    (c : DirectDegPoly D (D.m * D.d)) (t : DirectScalarQ D) :
   186	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   187	    directDiagonalAnswerEquiv D c (directScalarEquiv D t) =
   188	      directScalarEquiv D (evalCoefficient c t) := by
   189	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   190	  simp only [directDiagonalAnswerEquiv, DiagonalLinePolynomial.toFun,
   191	    evalLinePolynomialModel]
   192	  rw [show decodeScalar (directScalarEquiv D t) = t by
   193	    exact (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q)).symm_apply_apply t]
   194	  change encodeScalar ((coefficientPolynomial (D.m * D.d) c).eval t) =
   195	    directScalarEquiv D (evalCoefficient c t)
   196	  exact congrArg (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q))
   197	    (coefficientPolynomial_eval (D.m * D.d) c t)

   199	/-! ## Parameters and answers of the two QPBT game presentations -/
   200	
   201	/-- Forget the divisibility field and expose the directly indexed parameters. -/
   202	def LdParams.toDirectLdParams (L : LdParams) : DirectLdParams where
   203	  q := L.q
   204	  m := L.m
   205	  d := L.d
   206	  k := L.k
   207	  hm := L.hm
   208	  hd := L.hd
   209	  hk := L.hk
   210	  hq := L.hq

   212	@[simp] theorem LdParams.toDirectLdParams_model (L : LdParams) :
   213	    L.toDirectLdParams.model = L.model := by
   214	  unfold DirectLdParams.model LdParams.model LdParams.toDirectLdParams
   215	  congr
   216	
   217	/-- Constructor-preserving equivalence between answers of the seed-indexed
   218	and directly indexed QPBT games. -/
   219	noncomputable def ldDirectAnswerEquiv (L : LdParams) :
   220	    LdAnswer L ≃ DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams where
   221	  toFun
   222	    | .pointVals a => .pointVals a
   223	    | .alinePolys a => .alinePolys a
   224	    | .dlinePolys a => .dlinePolys a
   225	  invFun
   226	    | .pointVals a => .pointVals a
   227	    | .alinePolys a => .alinePolys a
   228	    | .dlinePolys a => .dlinePolys a
   229	  left_inv a := by cases a <;> rfl
   230	  right_inv a := by cases a <;> rfl

   232	/-! ## Parsing seed-indexed questions -/
   233	
   234	/-- Parse a seed-indexed question into the directly indexed question carrying
   235	the coordinate selected by `chiIndex`. -/
   236	noncomputable def parseLdQuestion (L : LdParams) :
   237	    LdQuestion L → DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams
   238	  | (.point, z) =>
   239	      (.point, ⟨z.point, L.toDirectLdParams.firstIndex, 0⟩)
   240	  | (.aline, z) =>
   241	      (.aline, ⟨z.point, chiIndex L z.seed, 0⟩)
   242	  | (.dline, z) =>
   243	      (.dline, ⟨z.point, chiIndex L z.seed, z.direction⟩)
   244	
   245	/-- Embed a direct sample into the seed-indexed ambient space using the
   246	specified residue in the selected seed fiber. -/
   247	noncomputable def ldSpaceOfDirectResidue (L : LdParams)
   248	    (sample : DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams)
   249	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) : LdSpace L
   250	  | .inl (.inl i) => sample.point i
   251	  | .inl (.inr _) => seedOfIndexResidue L sample.index residue
   252	  | .inr i => sample.direction i
   253	
   254	@[simp] theorem ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_point (L : LdParams)
   255	    (sample : DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams)
   256	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   257	    (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L sample residue).point = sample.point :=
   258	  rfl
   259	
   260	@[simp] theorem ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_seed (L : LdParams)
   261	    (sample : DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams)
   262	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   263	    (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L sample residue).seed =
   264	      seedOfIndexResidue L sample.index residue :=
   265	  rfl
   266	
   267	@[simp] theorem ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_direction (L : LdParams)
   268	    (sample : DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams)
   269	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   270	    (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L sample residue).direction = sample.direction :=
   271	  rfl
   272	
   273	/-- The ambient seed-indexed sample space is a direct sample together with a
   274	uniform residue in the selected seed fiber. -/
   275	noncomputable def ldSpaceSeedFiberEquiv (L : LdParams) :
   276	    LdSpace L ≃ DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams × Fin (L.q / L.m) where
   277	  toFun z :=
   278	    (⟨z.point, (seedFiberEquiv L z.seed).1, z.direction⟩,
   279	      (seedFiberEquiv L z.seed).2)
   280	  invFun x := ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L x.1 x.2
   281	  left_inv z := by
   282	    funext i
   283	    rcases i with (i | i)
   284	    · rcases i with (i | i)
   285	      · rfl
   286	      · rcases i with ⟨⟩
   287	        change (seedFiberEquiv L).symm (seedFiberEquiv L z.seed) = z.seed
   288	        exact (seedFiberEquiv L).symm_apply_apply z.seed
   289	    · rfl
   290	  right_inv x := by
   291	    rcases x with ⟨sample, residue⟩
   292	    apply Prod.ext
   293	    · cases sample with
   294	      | mk point index direction =>
   295	          simp only [ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_point,
   296	            ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_seed, ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_direction]
   297	          rw [seedFiberEquiv_seedOfIndexResidue]
   298	    · simp [seedOfIndexResidue]

   300	/-- Parsing a canonical seed-indexed question reconstructed from a direct
   301	sample gives exactly the corresponding direct canonical question. -/
   302	theorem parseLdQuestion_ldCL_ofDirectResidue (L : LdParams)
   303	    (t : LdType) (sample : DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams)
   304	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   305	    parseLdQuestion L
   306	        (t, ldCL L t (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L sample residue)) =

   309	  | point =>
   310	    rfl
   311	  | aline =>

   313	        simp only [parseLdQuestion, ldCL, ldALineCL, directLdMap,
   314	          ldSpaceOfDirectResidue, ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_point, LdSpace.seed,
   315	          chiIndex_seedOfIndexResidue]

   317	  | dline =>
   318	      ext <;>
   319	        simp only [parseLdQuestion, ldCL, ldDLineCL, directLdMap,

   321	          ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_direction, LdSpace.seed,
   322	          LdSpace.direction, chiIndex_seedOfIndexResidue,
   323	          prefixProjection]
   324	      rfl

   326	/-- The seed-indexed and direct predicates agree after parsing questions and
   327	transporting answers. -/
   328	theorem ldWinPredicate_parse (L : LdParams)
   329	    (x y : LdQuestion L) (a b : LdAnswer L) :
   330	    directLdWinPredicate L.toDirectLdParams
   331	        (parseLdQuestion L x) (parseLdQuestion L y)
   332	        (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L a) (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L b) =
   333	      ldWinPredicate L x y a b := by
   334	  rcases x with ⟨tx, x⟩
   335	  rcases y with ⟨ty, y⟩
   336	  cases tx <;> cases ty <;> cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl

   338	/-! ## Exact question-law transport -/
   339	
   340	/-- The common source sample is a direct common sample together with its
   341	uniform seed-fiber residue. -/
   342	noncomputable def ldQuestionSeedFiberEquiv (L : LdParams) :
   343	    ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace L) ≃
   344	      (((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams) ×
   345	        Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   346	  (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.refl (LdType × LdType))
   347	    (ldSpaceSeedFiberEquiv L)).trans
   348	      (Equiv.prodAssoc (LdType × LdType)
   349	        (DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams) (Fin (L.q / L.m))).symm
   350	
   351	/-- Forget the seed residue while retaining the ordered question types and
   352	the directly indexed common sample. -/
   353	noncomputable def ldQuestionSampleProjection (L : LdParams) :
   354	    ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace L) →
   355	      (LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams :=
   356	  fun source => (source.1, (ldSpaceSeedFiberEquiv L source.2).1)
   357	
   358	/-- Parse both questions in a seed-indexed question pair. -/
   359	noncomputable def parseLdQuestionPair (L : LdParams) :
   360	    (LdQuestion L × LdQuestion L) →
   361	      (DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams ×
   362	        DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams) :=
   363	  fun questions =>
   364	    (parseLdQuestion L questions.1, parseLdQuestion L questions.2)
   365	
   366	private theorem parse_ldQuestionSample (L : LdParams)
   367	    (source : (LdType × LdType) × LdSpace L) :
   368	    parseLdQuestionPair L
   369	        ((source.1.1, ldCL L source.1.1 source.2),
   370	          (source.1.2, ldCL L source.1.2 source.2)) =
   371	      let direct := ldQuestionSampleProjection L source
   372	      ((direct.1.1, directLdMap L.toDirectLdParams direct.1.1 direct.2),
   373	        (direct.1.2, directLdMap L.toDirectLdParams direct.1.2 direct.2)) := by
   374	  let sample := (ldSpaceSeedFiberEquiv L source.2).1
   375	  let residue := (ldSpaceSeedFiberEquiv L source.2).2
   376	  have hsource :
   377	      source.2 = ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L sample residue := by
   378	    exact (ldSpaceSeedFiberEquiv L).symm_apply_apply source.2 |>.symm
   379	  rw [hsource]
   380	  apply Prod.ext
   381	  · exact parseLdQuestion_ldCL_ofDirectResidue L source.1.1 sample residue
   382	  · exact parseLdQuestion_ldCL_ofDirectResidue L source.1.2 sample residue
   383	
   384	/-- Pushing the seed-indexed question law through the exact parser gives the
   385	directly indexed question law, including the ordered type-pair weights. -/
   386	theorem ldQuestionDistribution_map_parse (L : LdParams) :
   387	    (ldQuestionDistribution L).map (parseLdQuestionPair L) =
   388	      directLdQuestionDistribution L.toDirectLdParams := by
   389	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   390	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   391	  let sourceMap : ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace L) →
   392	      LdQuestion L × LdQuestion L := fun source =>
   393	    ((source.1.1, ldCL L source.1.1 source.2),
   394	      (source.1.2, ldCL L source.1.2 source.2))
   395	  let directMap :
   396	      ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams) →
   397	        DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams ×
   398	          DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams := fun source =>
   399	    ((source.1.1, directLdMap L.toDirectLdParams source.1.1 source.2),
   400	      (source.1.2, directLdMap L.toDirectLdParams source.1.2 source.2))
   401	  have huniform :
   402	      (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace L)).map
   403	          (ldQuestionSampleProjection L) =
   404	        uniformDistribution
   405	          ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams) := by
   406	    apply uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv (ldQuestionSeedFiberEquiv L)
   407	    intro source
   408	    rfl
   409	  calc
   410	    (ldQuestionDistribution L).map (parseLdQuestionPair L) =
   411	        (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace L)).map
   412	          (parseLdQuestionPair L ∘ sourceMap) := by
   413	      exact Distribution.map_map
   414	        (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace L))
   415	        sourceMap (parseLdQuestionPair L)
   416	    _ = (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace L)).map
   417	        (directMap ∘ ldQuestionSampleProjection L) := by
   418	      congr 1
   419	      funext source
   420	      exact parse_ldQuestionSample L source
   421	    _ = ((uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace L)).map
   422	          (ldQuestionSampleProjection L)).map directMap :=

    81	structure DirectLdSpace (D : DirectLdParams) where

    92	private def directLdSpacePointEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
    93	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
    94	      (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
    95	        (Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
    96	  toFun sample := (sample.point, sample.index, sample.direction)
    97	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.1, sample.2.1, sample.2.2⟩

   103	def directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :

   119	/-- Zero the coordinates preceding the directly sampled prefix index. -/
   120	def directPrefixProjection {D : DirectLdParams} (i : Fin D.m)
   121	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   122	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j

   124	/-- Canonical line descriptions whose coordinate index is stored directly.
   125	Coordinates are numbered from zero, so `index = i` represents coordinate
   126	`i + 1` in the paper. -/
   127	inductive DirectLineDesc (D : DirectLdParams) where
   128	  | axis (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   129	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection index) base = base)
   130	  | diagonal (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   131	      (direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
   132	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
   133	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < index.val → direction j = 0)

   136	/-- The kind of a directly indexed line. -/
   137	def DirectLineDesc.kind {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → LineKind

   139	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal

   141	/-- The coordinate index stored in a directly indexed line. -/
   142	def DirectLineDesc.index {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m

   144	  | .diagonal _ index _ _ _ => index
   145	
   146	/-- The canonical base point of a directly indexed line. -/
   147	def DirectLineDesc.base {D : DirectLdParams} :
   148	    DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
   149	  | .axis base _ _ => base
   150	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base

   152	/-- The geometric direction of a directly indexed line. -/
   153	def DirectLineDesc.direction {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   154	    Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=

   156	  | .axis _ index _ => coordinateDirection index
   157	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction

   159	/-- The base of a directly indexed description is fixed by its geometric

   161	theorem DirectLineDesc.base_fixed {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   162	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
   163	  cases line with
   164	  | axis base index baseFixed => exact baseFixed
   165	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
   166	
   167	/-- Every directly indexed diagonal description retains its prefix-zero

   169	theorem DirectLineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {D : DirectLdParams}

   172	  cases line with
   173	  | axis base index baseFixed => simp [DirectLineDesc.kind] at hline
   174	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero

   177	noncomputable def DirectLineDesc.pointSet {D : DirectLdParams}

   181	/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical axis-line description. -/
   182	noncomputable def directALineDescOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   183	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D) : DirectLineDesc D :=
   184	  let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
   185	  let base := lineRepMap direction sample.point
   186	  .axis base sample.index (lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point)
   187	
   188	/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical diagonal-line description. -/
   189	noncomputable def directDLineDescOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   190	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D) : DirectLineDesc D :=
   191	  let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
   192	  let base := lineRepMap direction sample.point
   193	  .diagonal base sample.index direction
   194	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point) (by
   195	      intro j hj
   196	      change directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction j = 0
   197	      rw [directPrefixProjection, if_pos hj])

   199	/-- The axis-line/point law with a directly sampled coordinate index. -/
   200	noncomputable def directALinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :

   206	noncomputable def directDLinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :

   226	theorem directDLinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :

   741	Since only admissible field sizes $q = 2^k$ arise in the Pauli basis test, the
   742	maximally entangled state $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ and the qudit Pauli
   743	projectors are isomorphic to tensor products of qubit EPR states
   744	$\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}$ and qubit Pauli projectors. This is the content of the
   745	next lemma, which is what allows the Pauli basis test to self-test Pauli
   746	observables and maximally entangled states over \emph{qubits}
   747	(Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}).
   748	
   749	\begin{lemma}[Qudit-to-qubit isomorphism]\label{lem:pauli-binary}
   750		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.qubitPauliProj, MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_qubitIsometry}
   751		\leanok
   752		\uses{def:admissible-size, def:subfields-kappa, def:binary-representation,
   753			def:generalized-pauli, def:EPR}
   754		For all admissible field sizes $q = 2^k$ and integers $L \ge 0$, there
   755		exists an isomorphism $\phi : (\C^q)^{\ot L} \to (\C^2)^{\ot Lk}$ such that
   756		\begin{equation}\label{eq:epr-q-to-epr-2}
   757			\phi \ot \phi\, \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot L}
   758			= \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}^{\ot Lk}
   759		\end{equation}
   760		(applying the natural identifications between
   761		$(\C^q)^{\ot L} \ot (\C^q)^{\ot L}$ and $(\C^q \ot \C^q)^{\ot L}$, and
   762		between $(\C^2)^{\ot Lk} \ot (\C^2)^{\ot Lk}$ and
   763		$(\C^2 \ot \C^2)^{\ot Lk}$). Moreover, for all $W \in \{X, Z\}$ and all
   764		$u \in \F_q^L$,
   765		\begin{equation}\label{eq:pauli-q-to-pauli-2}
   766			\tau^W_u = \phi^\dagger\,
   767			\Bigl(\bigotimes_{i=1}^L \bigotimes_{j=1}^k
   768			\sigma^W_{u_{ij}}\Bigr)\, \phi\;.
   769		\end{equation}
   770		Here $(u_{ij})_{i,j}$ is the array of $\F_2$ values with
   771		$u_i = \sum_j u_{ij} e_j$ for all $i \in \{1, \dots, L\}$, where
   772		$\{e_1, \dots, e_k\}$ is the fixed self-dual normal basis of $\F_q$ over
   773		$\F_2$ of Definition~\ref{def:binary-representation}; and for
   774		$i \in \{1, \dots, L\}$ and $j \in \{1, \dots, k\}$ the $(i,j)$-th factor
   775		$\sigma^W_{u_{ij}}$ denotes the projector
   776		$\frac{1}{2}\bigl(\Id + (-1)^{u_{ij}} \sigma^W(1)\bigr)$ acting on the
   777		$s$-th qubit, where $s = (i-1)k + j$.
   778		We index the product coordinates from zero: values $(i-1,j-1)$ correspond to
   779		the paper's pair $(i,j)$.  The corrected upper bound $j\leq k$ is
   780		documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_pauli-binary-factor-index}.
   781	\end{lemma}
   782	\begin{proof}
   783		\leanok
   784		\uses{def:binary-representation, def:subfields-kappa, lem:downsize_field,
   785			def:generalized-pauli, def:EPR, lem:pauli-observable-expansion}
   786		Let
   787		$e : \F_q^L \to \F_2^{L \times k}$ be the bijection that expands each
   788		coordinate in the fixed self-dual normal basis
   789		(Definition~\ref{def:binary-representation}), so that $e(u)$ is exactly the
   790		array $(u_{ij})_{i,j}$ of the statement, and let $\phi$ be the unitary that
   791		permutes the two computational bases along $e$, that is,
   792		$\phi \ket{u} = \ket{e(u)}$. Identity \eqref{eq:epr-q-to-epr-2} holds for
   793		any such relabelling: a bijection of orthonormal bases carries the maximally
   794		entangled state of the source space to that of the target space. For
   795		\eqref{eq:pauli-q-to-pauli-2}, conjugation by $\phi^\dagger$ is exactly
   796		the reindexing of a matrix along $e$, so it suffices to compare matrix
   797		entries. Both generalized Pauli observables are computed entrywise from
   798		Definition~\ref{def:generalized-pauli}: $\tau^W(a)$ is, for $W = X$, the
   799		permutation matrix of the translation $y \mapsto y + a$, and, for $W = Z$,
   800		the diagonal matrix with entries $(-1)^{\tr(a \cdot y)}$. The relabelling
   801		$e$ is additive, and item 2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_field} gives
   802		$\tr(a \cdot y) = e(a) \cdot e(y)$ by self-duality of the basis; the two
   803		entry formulas are therefore carried by the reindexing to the corresponding
   804		formulas over $\F_2$, so that $\tau^W(a)$ becomes $\tau^W(e(a))$ for both
   805		$W$. Finally, the projectors are recovered from the observables by the
   806		inversion identity \eqref{eq:pauli-inversion-0} in its characteristic-two
   807		form $\tau^W_u = \E_{\ba} (-1)^{\tr(\ba \cdot u)}\, \tau^W(\ba)$, used
   808		over $\F_q^L$ on the left-hand side and over $\F_2^{L \times k}$ on the
   809		right; averaging the entrywise comparison
   810		over $\ba$ carries $\tau^W_u$ to the qubit projector at the label
   811		$e(u) = \kappa(u)$, which is \eqref{eq:pauli-q-to-pauli-2}. This is the
   812		characteristic-two specialization of
   813		Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-observable-expansion}; the corresponding general-prime
   814		expansion and inversion are discussed in
   815		\cite{gap:qpbt_characteristic-two-pauli-scope}. The argument uses neither
   816		the qudit-by-qudit isometry $\theta$ of the source
   817		proof nor the product and twisted-commutation relations of
   818		Lemma~\ref{lem:twisted-commutation}.
   819	\end{proof}

   821	\begin{remark}\label{rem:pauli-binary-source}
   822		In the source statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-binary} in
   823		\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}, the index range of the qubit factor is printed as
   824		$j \in \{1, \dots, q\}$; the intended range, used above, is
   825		$j \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, as the $i$-th qudit is mapped to $k$ qubits. The
   826		source also quantifies over arbitrary integers $L$; the statement above
   827		takes $L$ to be a natural number, including zero, and uses the usual
   828		empty-product convention for the tensor powers when $L=0$.  The index
   829		correction is documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_pauli-binary-factor-index}.
   830	\end{remark}

    33	\section{Key theorem forms}
    34	Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb F_p$, let
    35	$\chi(x)=\exp(2\pi i\operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb F_p}(x)/p)$, and let
    36	$a,a',b\in K^n$.  The relevant identities are
    37	\[
    38	 \tau^W(a)\tau^W(a')=\tau^W(a+a'),\qquad
    39	 \tau^W(a)^p=I,
    40	\]
    41	and
    42	\[
    43	 \tau^X(a)\tau^Z(b)=\chi(-a\mathbin{\cdot}b)
    44	 \tau^Z(b)\tau^X(a).
    45	\]
    46	The explicit shift and phase matrices are unitary. The second identity implies
    47	that every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $\tau^W(a)$ satisfies $\lambda^p=1$. If
    48	$V\leq K^n$ and $v\notin V^\perp$, Fourier cancellation takes the form
    49	\[
    50	 \mathbb E_{u\in V}\chi(u\mathbin{\cdot}v)=0.
    51	\]
    52	Writing $P_b^W$ for the rank-one projector onto the $b$-labelled vector in the
    53	$W$ eigenbasis, the forward expansion and its Fourier inverse are
    54	\[
    55	 \tau^W(a)=\sum_{b\in K^n}\chi(a\mathbin{\cdot}b)P_b^W,
    56	 \qquad
    57	 P_b^W=\mathbb E_{a\in K^n}\chi(-a\mathbin{\cdot}b)\tau^W(a).
    58	\]

    60	\section{Source and formal scope}
    61	The source defines the shift and phase matrices and states their product,
    62	$p$-th-power, unitarity, spectral, and twisted-commutation properties in
    63	\cite[lines 1056--1095]{Ji2020MIPStar}. It uses the same character for Fourier
    64	cancellation over a subspace at lines 1124--1132.  The single-qudit forward and
    65	inverse expansions occur at lines 1118--1139, and their multi-qudit forms occur
    66	at lines 1151--1161.  These assertions use the characteristic-$p$ character;
    67	they are not intrinsically binary.
    68	
    69	The formal definitions \path{primeTauShift}, \path{primeTauPhase}, and
    70	\path{primeTauObservable} use the canonical character \path{ffChar} in
    71	characteristic $p$.  Their theorem statements cover the product, power,
    72	unitarity, spectral, commutation, and cancellation identities for arbitrary
    73	$p$.  The source-general forward expansion and inversion do not yet have
    74	corresponding Lean declarations.  Neither do the common eigenbases
    75	$\{\ket{b_W}\}$ and the rank-one projectors $P^W_b$ of the same source
    76	definition: these are formalized only in the characteristic-two form, by
    77	\path{pauliVec} and \path{pauliProj}, whose phases are given by
    78	\path{phaseSign}.  The general definition is therefore covered in Lean by its
    79	shift, phase, and observable matrices alone.  The declarations whose names begin with
    80	\path{tauObservable} or use \path{phaseSign} instead specialize to $p=2$, where
    81	$\chi(x)=(-1)^{\operatorname{Tr}(x)}$.  This specialization is appropriate only
    82	for the subsequent test, whose admissible sizes satisfy $q=2^k$; it is not
    83	substituted for the general statements.
    84	
    85	In characteristic two, $-x=x$, so the negative phase in the inverse expansion
    86	is the same \path{phaseSign} used in the forward expansion.  Thus
    87	\leanid{tauObservable\_eq\_sum\_pauliProj} and
    88	\leanid{pauliProj\_eq\_avg\_tauObservable} prove precisely the two displayed
    89	formulas for finite fields carrying an algebra over $\mathbb F_2$.  Their proof
    90	uses additive-character orthogonality after transporting the coordinate type
    91	along an equivalence with a finite ordinal; the restriction enters only through
    92	the identification of the canonical character with \path{phaseSign}.
    93	
    94	The proofs can be obtained directly from the displayed matrices.  A shift is a
    95	permutation matrix, a phase matrix has diagonal entries of modulus one, and a
    96	tensor product of such matrices is unitary.  Iterating the product identity
    97	gives $\tau^W(a)^p=I$.  Applying this equality to a nonzero eigenvector gives
    98	$(\lambda^p-1)v=0$, hence $\lambda^p=1$.  Finally, when
    99	$v\notin V^\perp$, the map $u\mapsto\chi(u\cdot v)$ is a nontrivial character
   100	of the finite additive group $V$, so its average vanishes.
   101	
   102	\section{Blueprint and formalization}
   103	The source-general definitions and results are recorded in
   104	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex} at
   105	\path{def:generalized-pauli}, \path{lem:twisted-commutation}, and
   106	\path{lem:pauli-observable-expansion}. Their Lean declarations are \leanid{primeTauShift},
   107	\leanid{primeTauPhase}, \leanid{primeTauObservable}, and the accompanying
   108	product, power, unitarity, spectral, commutation, and cancellation theorems.
   109	They quantify an arbitrary prime characteristic and use the corresponding
   110	additive character.
   111	
   112	The separately named binary declarations are used by the later QPBT chapters.
   113	In particular, \leanid{tauObservable\_eq\_sum\_pauliProj} is the forward
   114	observable expansion and \leanid{pauliProj\_eq\_avg\_tauObservable} is its
   115	normalized Fourier inverse.  They specialize the source formulas to
   116	characteristic two and are not linked as implementations of the unrestricted
   117	source node. Thus the blueprint, the general Lean interface, and the paper
   118	agree; the binary layer is a consumer specialization rather than a restriction
   119	of the source statement.
   120	
   121	\section{Conclusion}
   122	There is no mathematical restriction in the source-facing formal statements
   123	that exist: the shift, phase, and observable matrices retain arbitrary prime
   124	characteristic and the corresponding canonical character.  The eigenvectors and
   125	rank-one projectors of the same definition, however, exist only in the
   126	characteristic-two form, so the general definition is not yet covered in full.
   127	The characteristic-two declarations are separate corollaries for the QPBT
   128	parameter regime; the binary forward expansion and inversion are proved from
   129	the explicit matrices and character orthogonality.  The remaining work is to
   130	formalize and link the source-general eigenvectors, projectors, expansion, and
   131	inversion, and it does not require changing the binary operator definitions.

    33	/-! ## Heterogeneous extraction registers -/
    34	
    35	/-- One player's registers after adjoining the two generalized-Pauli
    36	registers: `AA'A''` or `BB'B''`. This identifies the register order and spaces for
    37	paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1429-1435,1687-1713` and
    38	blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:104-113,301-334`. -/
    39	abbrev ExtractionBlock (P : AdmissibleParams) (ι : Type*) :=
    40	  (ι × PauliRegister P) × PauliRegister P
    41	
    42	/-- The two heterogeneous extraction blocks in the order
    43	`AA'A'' | BB'B''`. This is the block presentation of the existing `SixReg`
    44	space used in `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
    45	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
    46	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
    47	abbrev ExtractionRegisters (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
    48	  ExtractionBlock P ιA × ExtractionBlock P ιB
    49	
    50	/-- The auxiliary registers `AA'BB'` occurring before the extracted EPR
    51	factor in `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`,
    52	paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
    53	abbrev ExtractionAuxRegisters (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
    54	  (ιA × PauliRegister P) × (ιB × PauliRegister P)
    55	
    56	/-- Reassociate the six-register order with the two extraction blocks.
    57	This equivalence identifies the register order in paper
    58	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1429-1435,1687-1713`. -/
    59	def sixRegExtractionEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    60	    SixReg P ιA ιB ≃ ExtractionRegisters P ιA ιB where
    61	  toFun p := (((p.1.1, p.1.2.1), p.1.2.2),
    62	    ((p.2.1, p.2.2.1), p.2.2.2))
    63	  invFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.1.2, p.1.2)),
    64	    (p.2.1.1, (p.2.1.2, p.2.2)))
    65	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    66	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    67	
    68	/-- Shuffle `AA'BB' | A''B''` into the six-register order. This equivalence
    69	places the ideal state in the order used in `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
    70	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
    71	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
    72	def extractionIdealShuffle (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    73	    (ExtractionAuxRegisters P ιA ιB ×
    74	      (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
    75	  toFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.1.2, p.2.1)),
    76	    (p.1.2.1, (p.1.2.2, p.2.2)))
    77	  invFun p := (((p.1.1, p.1.2.1), (p.2.1, p.2.2.1)),
    78	    (p.1.2.2, p.2.2.2))
    79	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    80	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl

    91	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by

    95	        (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)

   102	/-- Lift an operator on a player's original strategy register to that player's
   103	full extraction block. This places the Pauli and point measurements appearing

   105	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:177-205,348-375`. -/

   107	    (O : Op (S.LocalSpace side)) :
   108	    Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
   109	  heteroKron (heteroKron O 1) 1

   111	/-- Place an operator on the original strategy register of the selected
   112	player. This is the player-side placement used in `lem:qld-unitary`,
   113	blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`. -/
   114	noncomputable def placePlayer (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   115	    (O : Op (S.LocalSpace side)) :
   116	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
   117	  cases side with
   118	  | alice => exact S.place .AA' (heteroKron O 1)
   119	  | bob => exact S.place .BB' (heteroKron O 1)
   120	
   121	/-- Place an operator on the selected extracted register `A''` or `B''`.
   122	The unused strategy register in the crossed placement is assigned the
   123	identity. This is the placement of the ideal Pauli operators in
   124	`lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
   125	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   126	noncomputable def placeExtractedRegister (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   127	    (side : PlayerSide) (O : Op (PauliRegister P)) :
   128	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
   129	  cases side with
   130	  | alice =>
   131	      exact S.place .BA'' (heteroKron (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) O)
   132	  | bob =>
   133	      exact S.place .AB'' (heteroKron (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) O)
   134	
   135	/-- Place a pair of block operators simultaneously on `AA'A''` and
   136	`BB'B''`. This is the simultaneous placement used for the transformed state in
   137	`lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
   138	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   139	noncomputable def placeBoth (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   140	    (VA : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
   141	    (VB : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   142	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   143	  reindexOp (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   144	    (heteroKron VA VB)
   145	
   146	/-- Apply one operator to each heterogeneous extraction block. This is the
   147	witness-independent state transformation used for `V_A tensor V_B` in
   148	`lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
   149	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   150	noncomputable def applyBoth (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   151	    (VA : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
   152	    (VB : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB))
   153	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ
   154	      (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   155	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   156	  applyOperatorToState (S.placeBoth VA VB) ψ

   158	/-- The state `aux tensor EPR_q^{tensor M}` in the six-register order.
   159	This is the ideal state in Item 1 of `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
   160	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`, paper
   161	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   162	noncomputable def idealExpState (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)

blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:456:	In the source proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary}, the triangle inequality gives $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \| \leq \| (\Id - H_X)\ket{\vartheta} \| + \| (\Id - H_Z)\ket{\vartheta} \| \leq 2\sqrt{\delta_P}$, so that $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq 4\delta_P$; the source instead asserts the bound $2\sqrt{\delta_P}$ for the \emph{squared} norm, which holds only when $\sqrt{\delta_P} \leq 1/2$, and consequently carries the term $\sqrt{\delta_P}$ into an overlap bound of $1 - 2\delta_P - \sqrt{\delta_P}$.     29	\section{Key theorem forms: the printed statement}
    30	For $i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$, let $G^{i,x}$ be a projective measurement with
    31	outcome set $\mathcal G_i$. The source prints the sandwich as
    32	\[
    33	  G^{k,x}_{g_1}\cdots G^{1,x}_{g_k}\cdots G^{k,x}_{g_1}.
    34	\]
    35	This expression is not defined for a general family of outcome sets: the
    36	outer factor belongs to the measurement indexed by $\mathcal G_k$, whereas
    37	$g_1$ belongs to $\mathcal G_1$. The mismatch occurs in
    38	\cite[lines~465--501, especially lines~484--488]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
    39	
    40	The result is imported there from Fact~4.34 of the NEEXP paper
    41	\cite[lines~952--973, especially lines~965--968]{Natarajan2018NEEXP}, mirrored
    42	at \path{references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex}. That statement
    43	pairs every measurement with its own outcome, giving
    44	\[
    45	  G^{k,x}_{g_k}\cdots G^{2,x}_{g_2}G^{1,x}_{g_1}
    46	  G^{2,x}_{g_2}\cdots G^{k,x}_{g_k}.
    47	\]
    48	The order of the operators is unchanged; only the subscripts are corrected.
    49	
    50	\section{Blueprint and formalization}
    51	The blueprint uses the type-correct pairing at \path{lem:ld-sandwich} in
    52	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex} and explains the discrepancy
    53	in \path{rem:ld-sandwich-indexing}. The formal definition
    54	\leanid{sandwichProduct} uses an outcome function whose value at $i$ belongs
    55	to the outcome type of $G^i$. Thus every operator receives the corresponding
    56	component $g_i$. When $k=0$, the product is empty and its value is the identity,
    57	which supplies the unique empty-tuple outcome.

    60	The reversed outcome subscripts in the source are a typographical error, not a
    61	different mathematical construction. The blueprint and Lean statement retain
    62	the source's operator order while restoring the only type-correct pairing.

blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:545:	As printed in the source, the sandwich in Lemma~\ref{lem:ld-sandwich} pairs the $i$-th measurement with the outcome $g_{k+1-i}$: the outermost factor $G^{k,\,x}$ carries the outcome $g_1$ and the innermost factor $G^{1,\,x}$ carries $g_k$. The source also leaves the case $k = 0$ implicit; with the empty-product convention recorded in the statement, both sides of \eqref{eq:ld-sandwich-2} are then the identity on the single empty-tuple outcome and the conclusion holds with error zero.  The correction is documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-sandwich-indexing}.
